One review mentions a booking-time mix-up that the team resolved by working diligently past closing. Session information is on the official site, colorsignal.co.kr. sparex-sauna-good-morning-city-dongmyo.name: SPAREX Sauna (Good Morning City)
sparex-sauna-good-morning-city-dongmyo.summary: The Sparex chain's Good Morning City branch — three levels under the mall, a minute from Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station.
sparex-sauna-good-morning-city-dongmyo.longDescription:
SPAREX's Good Morning City branch is on the third basement level of the Good Morning City mall, at 247 Jangchungdan-ro in Jung-gu, about a minute from Exit 14 of Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station on Line 4.

It is a jjimjilbang rather than a private spa — the communal bathhouse format, with wet and dry saunas, a restaurant, sleeping areas and luggage storage, and jjimjil clothes and a towel included with entry. The rest areas are done in a hanok concept, including small pavilion-style spaces off the common floor. It runs 24 hours a day, year round, though the body-scrub service pauses between 01:00 and 03:00 for cleaning.

Sparex runs a second Seoul branch nearby, at Dongmyoap Station in Jongno-gu; it is listed here separately as SPAREX Sauna (Dongmyo).

korean-home-style-cooking-class-near-gan.summary: Home-style Korean cooking near Gangnam Station — creative freedom over strict recipes, with the culture behind each dish.
korean-home-style-cooking-class-near-gan.whyWeLikeIt: Rather than marching through a fixed recipe, the class leaves room to improvise, and reviewers value learning the cultural background of each ingredient. A 4.9 rating across 80 reviews backs it up.
korean-home-style-cooking-class-near-gan.longDescription:
This home-style class near Gangnam Station takes a loose approach to recipes: rather than following one line by line, participants are given room to improvise while preparing a main dish alongside several banchan. Along the way, the cultural background of each ingredient is explained, so the session doubles as a small lesson in Korean food culture.

It holds a 4.9 rating across 80 reviews, and the location by Gangnam Station makes it straightforward to reach by subway.

kimchi-making-class-with-chef-hakyung-at.name: Kimchi Class with Chef Hakyung
kimchi-making-class-with-chef-hakyung-at.summary: Kimchi-making class with Chef Hakyung near Gyeongbokgung.
kimchi-making-class-with-chef-hakyung-at.longDescription: Led by Chef Hakyung, this kimchi-making class takes place near Gyeongbokgung Palace in Jongno-gu, in the Bukchon area. The session is devoted entirely to kimchi, and the location is simple to pair with a morning at the palace or a walk through Bukchon afterward.

cooking-class-in-mangwon-market-with-mic.name: Mangwon Market Chef's Cooking Class
cooking-class-in-mangwon-market-with-mic.summary: Shop Mangwon Market with a Michelin-experienced chef, then cook what you found — closer to cultural exchange than a lesson.
cooking-class-in-mangwon-market-with-mic.bestFor: market-to-table cooking with a professional chef
cooking-class-in-mangwon-market-with-mic.whyWeLikeIt: Reviewers describe it as closer to cultural exchange than a lesson — shopping Mangwon Market with Chef Pano before cooking together — and the clean, spacious studio draws its own praise.
cooking-class-in-mangwon-market-with-mic.longDescription:
At Mangwon Market in Mapo-gu, Chef Pano — a chef with Michelin restaurant experience — begins the class with a walk through the market stalls, shopping for the day's ingredients before heading back to cook them together. Reviewers describe the format as closer to a cultural exchange than a formal lesson, and note that the studio is clean and spacious.

The class holds a 5.0 rating across 28 reviews; updates are posted on Instagram at @seoulfoodventure and @seoulcookingclub.

korean-cooking-class-with-grocery-shoppi.name: Market-to-Table Cooking Class
korean-cooking-class-with-grocery-shoppi.summary: Korean cooking class that starts with grocery shopping in Mangwon Market.
korean-cooking-class-with-grocery-shoppi.bestFor: shopping and cooking like a local
korean-cooking-class-with-grocery-shoppi.longDescription: The session begins not at a stove but in the aisles of Mangwon Market in Mapo-gu, where participants shop for groceries before cooking a Korean meal with what they found. It is a straightforward market-to-table format; plan for the shopping portion as part of the class time rather than a separate activity.

kimchi-cooking-class-in-traditional-hano.name: Hanok Kimchi Cooking Class
kimchi-cooking-class-in-traditional-hano.summary: Kimchi class held in a traditional hanok near Bukchon.
kimchi-cooking-class-in-traditional-hano.bestFor: making kimchi inside a traditional hanok
kimchi-cooking-class-in-traditional-hano.longDescription: Held in a traditional hanok house in Jongno-gu, near Bukchon and Gyeongbokgung, this class is devoted to a single subject: kimchi. The hanok venue is the distinguishing detail, and the location keeps the palace and the rest of Bukchon close at hand.

royal-seoul-cooking-class-in-a-100-year-.name: Royal Seoul Cooking Class
royal-seoul-cooking-class-in-a-100-year-.summary: Royal Korean cooking in a 100-year-old hanok, paired with a market tour.
royal-seoul-cooking-class-in-a-100-year-.bestFor: royal recipes and a market tour
royal-seoul-cooking-class-in-a-100-year-.whyWeLikeIt: Ninety-eight reviewers rate it 5.0, with particular praise for the instructors' background knowledge and considerate pacing.
royal-seoul-cooking-class-in-a-100-year-.longDescription:
A century-old hanok in the Bukchon area is the setting for this class, which pairs royal-style Korean cooking with a tour of a local market. Reviewers praise the instructors — Park is mentioned by name — for their depth of background knowledge and considerate pacing.

It holds a 5.0 rating across 98 reviews, and the hanok sits near Gyeongbokgung in Jongno-gu, so it combines easily with a palace visit. Updates are posted at @royalseoulcc on Instagram.

traditional-korean-6-dish-cooking-class-.name: Korean 6-Dish Class & Alley Tour
traditional-korean-6-dish-cooking-class-.summary: Six-dish traditional Korean cooking class plus a hidden-alley walking tour.
traditional-korean-6-dish-cooking-class-.bestFor: a full Korean table plus neighborhood walk
traditional-korean-6-dish-cooking-class-.longDescription: Six traditional Korean dishes are on the menu here, cooked in a single session before the group heads out for a walking tour of alleys near Bukchon and Gyeongbokgung in Jongno-gu. Because the class and the tour come as one combined program, plan your schedule around both parts rather than the cooking alone.

seoul-soju-makgeolli-tasting-experience.name: Soju & Makgeolli Tasting
seoul-soju-makgeolli-tasting-experience.summary: Soju and makgeolli tastings, from distillery visits to guided flights.
seoul-soju-makgeolli-tasting-experience.bestFor: a guided introduction to soju and makgeolli
seoul-soju-makgeolli-tasting-experience.longDescription:
These tastings introduce Korea's traditional alcohols — soju and makgeolli — in formats that range from guided flights to distillery visits in Seoul. Session titles such as "Seoul Soju Tasting at Distillery" and "Discover Traditional Soju & Makgeolli" give a sense of the spread on offer.

Because the formats differ, it is worth confirming whether your session is a seated tasting or a distillery visit before you book.

where-locals-eat-korean-bbq-dry-aged-han.name: Where Locals Eat: Korean BBQ
where-locals-eat-korean-bbq-dry-aged-han.summary: Hosted Korean BBQ and dry-aged hanwoo dinners where locals actually eat.
where-locals-eat-korean-bbq-dry-aged-han.bestFor: diners curious about dry-aged hanwoo beef
where-locals-eat-korean-bbq-dry-aged-han.longDescription:
Hosted dinners built around Korean BBQ and dry-aged hanwoo beef, held at the kind of restaurants where locals actually eat. Formats vary — listings such as "Korean BBQ of the Month," "Private Korean BBQ with Jason," and "A Gourmet Korean BBQ & Dry-Aged Hanwoo" suggest both private and gourmet-dinner versions of the experience.

One practical note: the venue's location is not publicly disclosed, so plan around receiving the specifics through the booking rather than mapping it out in advance.

brewing-makgeolli-experience.name: Makgeolli Brewing Experience
brewing-makgeolli-experience.summary: Brew your own makgeolli in a Seongsu workshop.
brewing-makgeolli-experience.bestFor: brewing your own Korean rice wine
brewing-makgeolli-experience.longDescription: Over in Seongsu-dong, Seongdong-gu, this workshop centers on brewing makgeolli, Korea's traditional rice wine, and each participant makes their own batch. As a traditional-liquor workshop rather than a cooking class in the usual sense, it suits visitors who have already tried a kimchi or banchan class and want to go one step further.

the-seoul-pub-crawl.name: The Seoul Pub Crawl
the-seoul-pub-crawl.summary: Itaewon-based pub crawl through Seoul's nightlife.
the-seoul-pub-crawl.bestFor: a sociable evening out in Itaewon
the-seoul-pub-crawl.longDescription: Based in Itaewon, in Yongsan-gu, this pub crawl moves a group through Seoul's nightlife over the course of an evening and currently holds a 4.7 rating. Published details beyond the Itaewon base are limited, so check the current schedule and meeting point when booking — and expect a late-night, social format rather than a quiet tasting.

gwangjang-market-half-day-street-food-ex.name: Gwangjang Street Food Tour
gwangjang-market-half-day-street-food-ex.summary: Half-day Gwangjang Market street-food tour run like a stamp-rally challenge — guides get repeat praise.
gwangjang-market-half-day-street-food-ex.bestFor: a first guided taste of Gwangjang Market
gwangjang-market-half-day-street-food-ex.whyWeLikeIt: Reviewers keep returning to the guides — Cecilia's local knowledge and friendliness come up again and again — and the tour holds a 4.9 rating across 179 reviews.
gwangjang-market-half-day-street-food-ex.longDescription:
A half-day tour through Gwangjang Market in Jongno, structured as a stamp-rally challenge that works through the market's signature street foods, with a souvenir folded into the format. This is Klook's own tour, booked directly through that platform.

With a 4.9 rating across 179 reviews, and guides repeatedly praised for their local knowledge and warmth, it offers a structured way to take on the market rather than guessing on your own. Set aside a half day for the full route.

gwangjang-market-half-day-vegan-food-tou.name: Gwangjang Vegan Food Tour
gwangjang-market-half-day-vegan-food-tou.summary: Half-day vegan food tour through Gwangjang Market.
gwangjang-market-half-day-vegan-food-tou.longDescription:
Plant-based visitors get a route of their own through Gwangjang Market with this half-day tour, which currently holds a 5.0 rating. The premise is straightforward: a guided walk through the Jongno market focused entirely on vegan food.

Published details are otherwise limited, so confirm the current lineup of stops — and any dietary specifics that matter to you — directly when booking.

absolute-seoul-pub-crawl-hongdae-itaewon.name: Absolute Seoul Pub Crawl
absolute-seoul-pub-crawl-hongdae-itaewon.summary: High-energy pub crawl with hosts who mix an international crowd — Hongdae most nights, Itaewon on Fridays.
absolute-seoul-pub-crawl-hongdae-itaewon.bestFor: meeting fellow travelers on a night out
absolute-seoul-pub-crawl-hongdae-itaewon.whyWeLikeIt: With a 4.8 rating across 263 reviews, the crawl is praised for local hosts who run the night with real energy and pull travelers of many nationalities into one group.
absolute-seoul-pub-crawl-hongdae-itaewon.longDescription:
Absolute Seoul Pub Crawl runs on a fixed weekly rhythm: Hongdae on Thursdays, Saturdays, and Sundays, and Itaewon on Fridays. Local hosts keep the energy high and mix travelers of many nationalities into one group — reviewers describe it as much a way to meet fellow travelers as a bar tour.

The crawl has a website at seoulpubcrawl.com and an Instagram account at @absolutekorea; check which district is on before you head out, since the night's location depends on the day of the week.

olive-young-n-seongsu.name: Olive Young N Seongsu
olive-young-n-seongsu.summary: Olive Young's five-floor innovation flagship, opened in late 2024 near Seongsu Station — the chain's biggest bet yet on what a K-beauty store can be.
olive-young-n-seongsu.bestFor: a one-stop overview of what's trending across Korean beauty right now
olive-young-n-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: It's less a bigger branch than a lab for the brand's next store format, with each floor built around a different way of shopping rather than just more shelves.
olive-young-n-seongsu.longDescription:
Olive Young N Seongsu opened in November 2024 as the chain's first entry in a new 'innovation store' concept, spread across five floors near Exit 4 of Seongsu Station. Where a standard Olive Young branch is organized by product category, this flagship is organized by experience — different floors are built around different ways of browsing and testing K-beauty products.

As the format-setter for where Olive Young's retail concept is headed next, it's worth the detour even for travelers who've already been to a dozen branches elsewhere in Seoul.

amore-seongsu.name: Amore Seongsu
amore-seongsu.summary: Amorepacific's flagship experience space in a converted repair shop — test 2,000+ products across 30+ brands, no checkout pressure.
amore-seongsu.bestFor: Trying the whole Amorepacific universe before you buy
amore-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: It's built as a showroom, not a store — plus free luggage lockers, which every carry-on traveler eventually thanks them for.
amore-seongsu.longDescription:
Amore Seongsu occupies a former auto repair shop converted into Amorepacific's group-wide showroom, letting visitors test products from more than 30 of the company's brands in one open space rather than shopping brand by brand. With well over 2,000 products on hand, it's built for exploration rather than a fast checkout.

Free luggage lockers make it a practical stop mid-itinerary, and the space sits alongside several other beauty and fashion flagships on Seongsu's Yeonmujang-area streets.

tamburins-seongsu.name: Tamburins Seongsu
tamburins-seongsu.summary: A raw-concrete flagship built around Tamburins' perfumes, hand creams, and rotating art installations, on one of Seongsu's original converted-warehouse streets.
tamburins-seongsu.bestFor: browsing niche Korean fragrance without a hard sell
tamburins-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: The architecture is the draw as much as the products — the cave-like concrete interior has made it a fixture in Seongsu's design-tourism circuit since it opened.
tamburins-seongsu.longDescription:
Tamburins Seongsu is the fragrance and cosmetics brand's flagship on Yeonmujang 5-gil, built inside a raw-concrete structure that leans as hard into architecture as it does into product. Alongside the brand's perfumes, hand creams, and body care, the space regularly hosts art installations that change out the interior look.

It's open daily from 11am to 9pm, a few minutes from Seongsu Station Exit 4, and works well paired with the other flagship stores clustered on the same block.

nonfiction-seongsu.name: Nonfiction Seongsu
nonfiction-seongsu.summary: A minimalist showroom for Nonfiction's fragrance and skincare line, with open counters built for unhurried testing rather than a quick grab-and-go.
nonfiction-seongsu.bestFor: sampling Nonfiction's signature scents at your own pace
nonfiction-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: The pared-back, gallery-like layout matches the brand's whole aesthetic — it reads more like a design showroom than a retail counter.
nonfiction-seongsu.longDescription:
Nonfiction's Seongsu store is one of more than ten global locations for the fragrance and skincare brand, but it's the flagship showroom for Seoul. The interior favors open testing counters and a restrained material palette over dense product walls, in keeping with the brand's minimalist identity.

It keeps daily hours from 11am to 8:30pm and sits a short walk from Tamburins and other Seongsu flagships, making it an easy stop on a fragrance-focused route through the neighborhood.

tirtir-seongsu.name: TIRTIR Seongsu
tirtir-seongsu.summary: TIRTIR's two-floor flagship, built around its cult-favorite cushion foundation shade range — five distinct zones for matching your exact tone before you buy.
tirtir-seongsu.bestFor: finding your shade match among TIRTIR's wide cushion foundation range
tirtir-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: The 'Shade Valley' concept turns a task that's usually a guessing game online — picking the right cushion shade — into something you can actually test in person.
tirtir-seongsu.longDescription:
TIRTIR Seongsu opened in mid-2025 as the brand's flagship, spread across a basement and ground floor near Seongsu Station on Yeonmujang 5-gil. The store is organized into five themed zones under a 'Shade Valley' concept, built specifically around trying the brand's wide range of cushion foundation shades in person.

The store passed its first anniversary with a dedicated event, a reasonable signal it's a standing flagship rather than a short-lived promotional pop-up. Hours run 10:30am to 8:30pm daily.

amuse-seongsu.name: Amuse Seongsu
amuse-seongsu.summary: Amuse's all-pink 'Pink House' flagship — a full brand-world showroom for its vegan, jelly-textured makeup line, opened in mid-2025.
amuse-seongsu.bestFor: the most photographed makeup showroom in Seongsu right now
amuse-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: It commits fully to one color story instead of splitting the difference, which makes it read as a genuine brand statement rather than a generic pop-up shell.
amuse-seongsu.longDescription:
Amuse opened its Seongsu flagship — nicknamed 'Pink House' — in June 2025, its second flagship store after an earlier Hongdae location. The roughly 200-square-meter space is built entirely around the brand's signature pink and its vegan, jelly-textured makeup and skincare line.

Expect a dense photo-op interior alongside testing stations for Amuse's core products; it's a quick stop rather than a long browse, but a distinctive one on a Seongsu beauty crawl.

fwee-seongsu.name: fwee Seongsu
fwee-seongsu.summary: fwee's first offline store, nicknamed 'AGIT' — built around testing its full lip-tint and pudding-pot color range in one blue-toned space.
fwee-seongsu.bestFor: swatching fwee's full lip color lineup in one visit
fwee-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: Dozens of shades laid out for open testing is a genuinely useful format for a brand best known online for color range — you can actually compare them side by side here.
fwee-seongsu.longDescription:
fwee AGIT Seongsu, opened in February 2024, is the makeup brand's first permanent offline store after a run of pop-ups, including one at The Hyundai Seoul. The store leans into fwee's signature blue on its exterior and gives shoppers open access to test dozens of lip product shades and the brand's full pudding pot lineup.

It keeps year-round daily hours from 11am to 9pm and sits a short walk from several of Seongsu's other beauty flagships, making it easy to fold into a same-day beauty-store route.

musinsa-standard-seongsu.name: Musinsa Standard Seongsu
musinsa-standard-seongsu.summary: The physical storefront for Musinsa's in-house basics label, letting you check sizing and fabric on pieces most travelers only know from the app.
musinsa-standard-seongsu.bestFor: checking Musinsa Standard sizing and fit before ordering more online
musinsa-standard-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: It turns Korea's biggest fashion platform from a screen into a fitting room — genuinely useful if you plan to keep shopping Musinsa's app after you fly home.
musinsa-standard-seongsu.longDescription:
Musinsa Standard Seongsu is the two-floor retail store for Musinsa's own basics line, part of a broader wave of offline stores the online platform has opened in the neighborhood alongside its larger Musinsa Megastore Seongsu. The space stocks minimalist, everyday casualwear in neutral colorways, the label's signature look.

It's open daily from 11am to 9pm with tax-free service for international visitors, making it a practical stop if you already shop the Musinsa app and want to check fit in person.

ader-error-seongsu.name: Ader Error Seongsu Space
ader-error-seongsu.summary: Ader Error's flagship since 2020, renovated for the brand's 10th anniversary into a chrome-and-glass, gallery-like two-floor space.
ader-error-seongsu.bestFor: seeing Ader Error's off-kilter design language applied to a whole building, not just a rack of clothes
ader-error-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: The renovation treats the store as an art installation first and a shop second, which fits a brand that's always blurred the line between fashion and conceptual art.
ader-error-seongsu.longDescription:
ADER Space has anchored Ader Error's presence in Seongsu since 2020, and was fully renovated in late 2024 for the brand's tenth anniversary under the theme 'FUTOURIST.' The redesign leans into glass and chrome finishes with undulating interiors and futuristic fixtures across two floors, alongside the brand's ready-to-wear and accessories.

Open daily from 1pm to 9pm, it's one of the longer-standing flagships in the neighborhood rather than a newcomer, and rewards a slower browse over a quick in-and-out.

lcdc-seoul.name: LCDC Seoul
lcdc-seoul.summary: A four-floor complex stacking a café, a multi-brand select shop, and several independent fashion labels under one roof — Seongsu's version of a vertical mall.
lcdc-seoul.bestFor: browsing several independent Korean fashion labels without hopping between separate stores
lcdc-seoul.whyWeLikeIt: Each floor has its own distinct identity instead of blending into one generic retail floor, so it rewards working your way up rather than just hitting the ground level.
lcdc-seoul.longDescription:
LCDC Seoul stacks a ground-floor café (Cafe Ephemera) with a curated multi-brand select shop on the second floor and several independent labels — including Doors, Geulwoll, and Apoteka Soul — sharing the third, plus a jewelry-and-accessories floor above. The building itself, a converted structure on Yeonmujang 17-gil, is part of the draw alongside what's inside it.

Hours vary a little by floor, roughly 10am to 9pm depending on the tenant, with valet parking available — useful given how spread out Seongsu's flagship stores are.

eql-grove-seongsu.name: EQL Grove
eql-grove-seongsu.summary: EQL's offline entry point into Seongsu, an 'editorial forest' select shop that brings the online platform's curated fashion picks into a physical space with rotating local brand collaborations.
eql-grove-seongsu.bestFor: discovering smaller Korean labels alongside EQL's own curated picks
eql-grove-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: It functions as a community space as much as a shop — the rotating collaborations with local Seongsu brands give it a reason to check back on repeat visits.
eql-grove-seongsu.longDescription:
EQL Grove brought the online curated-fashion platform EQL into a physical Seongsu storefront, styled as an 'editorial forest' that showcases items previously only available through the app. Beyond straightforward shopping, the space runs themed promotions and collaborations with other local Seongsu brands.

It's open daily from 11am to 8pm, closed on Korean public holidays, and works well as a stop for travelers who want a curated, editor's-pick alternative to the bigger flagship stores nearby.

matin-kim-seongsu.name: Matin Kim Seongsu
matin-kim-seongsu.summary: Matin Kim's Seongsu flagship for the label's oversized, Y2K-leaning streetwear — one of several Seoul stores, but the one built as a full brand-world showroom.
matin-kim-seongsu.bestFor: trying on Matin Kim's oversized silhouettes in person before buying online
matin-kim-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: It's one of Matin Kim's larger physical footprints, worth the trip if you already follow the brand's fast-moving online drops and want to check fit for yourself.
matin-kim-seongsu.longDescription:
Matin Kim runs several storefronts across Seongsu, and this flagship on Yeonmujang 3-gil is the label's main showroom for the neighborhood, alongside smaller branch and special-edition stores nearby. The brand is known for oversized, Y2K-inflected streetwear that moves quickly through frequent online drops.

Seeing the fit and fabric in person is the main draw here, since Matin Kim's popularity online means pieces can sell out fast — a fitting-room visit is a low-risk way to confirm sizing before committing to a purchase.

onion-seongsu.name: Onion Seongsu
onion-seongsu.summary: The original Onion — a converted factory turned bakery café that's widely credited with kicking off Seongsu's transformation into Seoul's café district.
onion-seongsu.bestFor: warehouse-industrial atmosphere plus a genuinely strong bakery counter
onion-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: It predates most of the cafés that copied its look, and it still bakes well enough to be worth the visit even without the exposed-brick backdrop.
onion-seongsu.longDescription:
Onion Seongsu occupies a former factory building and is often credited as the café that put Seongsu-dong on the map as a destination neighborhood, well before the area filled with flagship fashion stores. The bakery counter, not just the industrial-chic interior, is the reason regulars keep returning — bread and pastries sell out on busy days.

It opens earlier than most Seongsu cafés, from 8am on weekdays and 10am on weekends, both running until 10pm — useful if you want to beat the crowds that build later in the day.

mesh-coffee.name: Mesh Coffee
mesh-coffee.summary: A compact, takeout-only hand-drip specialty bar near Seoul Forest — no seating, just a tight focus on the coffee itself.
mesh-coffee.bestFor: a quick, high-quality coffee stop on the walk to or from Seoul Forest
mesh-coffee.whyWeLikeIt: Dropping seating entirely lets it focus purely on the brew — a useful counterpoint if you've spent the day in Seongsu's photo-op cafés and just want good coffee, fast.
mesh-coffee.longDescription:
Mesh Coffee is a small, takeout-only specialty bar between Seoul Forest and Ttukseom Station, built around hand-drip coffee rather than a sit-down café experience. There's no indoor seating, so it works best as a stop on the way to or from Seoul Forest park rather than a destination to linger at.

Weekday hours run 10am to 6pm; the matcha latte and Americano are the most-mentioned menu items, and its small footprint means it can get busy quickly around peak café-hopping hours.

in-the-pink-seongsu.name: In The Pink Seongsu
in-the-pink-seongsu.summary: An English-first personal color studio in Seongsu, run by a bilingual founder who has draped 9,000-plus clients through a 350-plus-swatch process.
in-the-pink-seongsu.bestFor: travelers who want the whole session — booking form to drape to breakdown — handled comfortably in English
in-the-pink-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: Founder Nicole built the entire booking flow, and the FAQ that explains bare-face draping, around clients who don't speak Korean — down to the wording of the questions people actually ask before a session.
in-the-pink-seongsu.longDescription:
In The Pink is a personal color studio in Seongsu run by Nicole, a certified color consultant and fashion stylist who has led personal color workshops abroad through the Korean Cultural Center, including stops in Hungary, the UK, the Czech Republic, Italy, and Spain. Sessions center on a bare-face draping process using more than 350 fabric swatches to identify a client's undertone, then extend into recommendations for makeup shades, hairstyle and color, glasses frames, and fabric choices.

Booking runs through a form-and-email flow rather than a walk-in counter, with 1:1 sessions lasting about 80 minutes and paired sessions running longer — all explained in English from the FAQ onward, which is unusual for the format in Seongsu. The studio's exact address isn't published online; it's shared directly with clients once a booking is confirmed.

ccl-color-lab-seongsu.name: CCL Color Image Convergence Lab
ccl-color-lab-seongsu.summary: A personal-color and image-consulting lab near Seoul Forest, run out of its own Seongsu studio with a full program menu from color draping to body-frame styling.
ccl-color-lab-seongsu.bestFor: a deeper consulting menu — color, body-frame styling, and makeup — under one roof rather than a single-service session
ccl-color-lab-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: CCL also runs its own academy arm and holds patent registrations for its diagnostic tools, so the person draping you has typically also trained other colour consultants in the method.
ccl-color-lab-seongsu.longDescription:
CCL (컬러이미지융합연구소) runs its personal color studio out of the Seoul Forest Dream Tower in Seongsu, a short walk from Seoul Forest itself. Alongside its core personal color consulting program, the lab offers a men's-focused diagnosis track, body-frame and fit styling, makeup consulting, and color therapy sessions.

What sets it apart from single-session studios nearby is the academy side of the business — CCL holds its own patent registrations for diagnostic tools and issues its own counselor certifications through a dedicated training arm. Sessions can be booked through its Instagram (@cclcolor_official) or arranged directly through the studio.

5x5-nail-studio-seongsu.name: 5x5 Nail Studio Seongsu
5x5-nail-studio-seongsu.summary: A high-following nail art studio in Seongsu known for nature-inspired custom designs — marble, stone, and watercolor motifs — booked entirely through Instagram.
5x5-nail-studio-seongsu.bestFor: elaborate custom nail art booked in advance, with English-speaking staff on hand
5x5-nail-studio-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: The studio keeps separate accounts for its class offerings and design archive, a level of documentation that's closer to a working design studio than a typical walk-in nail shop.
5x5-nail-studio-seongsu.longDescription:
5x5 Nail Studio (오오네일) runs two Seoul locations, one in Seongsu and one in Yeonnam, and has built a large following around nature-inspired nail art — marble, stone-texture, and watercolor motifs among its signature styles. Appointments, which typically run about an hour to ninety minutes depending on the design, are arranged through Instagram DM or KakaoTalk rather than a booking site.

English-speaking staff support the international clients who make up a large share of its bookings, and the studio maintains sister accounts for its class offerings and design archive — worth a browse before messaging to book, since custom pieces are usually chosen from a reference photo.

dakyo-nail-seongsu.name: Dakyo Nail Seongsu
dakyo-nail-seongsu.summary: The Seongsu branch of the Dakyo Nail family, a K-pop-adjacent nail art studio with its own account and following distinct from the brand's Hannam and Apgujeong locations.
dakyo-nail-seongsu.bestFor: trend-driven, idol-inspired nail art in the style Dakyo Nail is known for
dakyo-nail-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: Being the Seongsu outpost of a multi-branch brand means near-daily fresh design uploads on its own account — a useful scroll for style references before you message to book.
dakyo-nail-seongsu.longDescription:
Dakyo Nail Seongsu (다교네일 성수) is one of several branches under the Dakyo Nail name, a nail art brand also operating in Hannam-dong and — separately from this Seongsu shop — Apgujeong. The Seongsu location runs its own Instagram account distinct from the brand's main and representative accounts, posting frequent updates on current nail art designs.

As with most Seongsu nail studios of this type, booking runs through Instagram DM or a linked Kakao channel rather than a website, and the shop sits in a commercial building on Yeonmujang 15-gil in the heart of the neighborhood's studio cluster.

soonsiki-seongsu.name: Soonsiki Seongsu
soonsiki-seongsu.summary: The Seongsu branch of Soonsiki, a multi-location Seoul hair chain built around English-friendly service for international guests.
soonsiki-seongsu.bestFor: a full-service cut, color, or perm handled by a chain that markets its English-friendliness up front
soonsiki-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: Soonsiki brands its English-friendly service and multi-branch consistency directly on its own site rather than leaving it to a DM negotiation, which is unusual for a Seongsu salon at this scale.
soonsiki-seongsu.longDescription:
Soonsiki Seongsu (순시키헤어 성수 샤미즈점) is one of four Seoul locations run under the Soonsiki name, occupying the 4th and 5th floors of a building on Yeonmujang 3-gil, alongside sibling branches in Hongdae. The chain has built its identity around serving international guests specifically, branding itself as English-friendly across its locations.

Booking runs through the salon's own site or its Instagram (@soonsiki.official), and the Seongsu branch keeps the same Wednesday–Sunday, 10am–7pm schedule as the rest of the chain, closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

a-knack.name: A KNACK Seongsu
a-knack.summary: A cut-focused Seongsu salon built around structural, sculptural styling, with a scalp head-spa treatment on the side.
a-knack.bestFor: a precision, design-led cut from a Seongsu specialist, with a head-spa add-on if you want one
a-knack.whyWeLikeIt: Design-forward Seongsu hair salon known for structured cuts that also offers head-spa scalp treatments for scalp and hair fatigue recovery.
a-knack.longDescription:
A KNACK (어냅) is a cut-focused hair salon on Seongsu-il-ro 1-gil, in the middle of Seongsu's café-and-boutique cluster. The shop is known for structural, sculptural styles — two-block cuts, blunt bobs, hime cuts — finished with highlights and braiding for emphasis, under stylist Kim Ji-eun, who frames the salon's approach as blending newness with everyday wearability.

Beyond cuts, A KNACK also runs a scalp head-spa treatment aimed at relieving buildup and hair fatigue, rounding it out beyond a straightforward cut shop. Hours run 10am–7pm, closed Mondays and Tuesdays, with booking through Instagram rather than a dedicated site.

you-hair-salon-seongsu.name: YOU Hair Salon Seongsu
you-hair-salon-seongsu.summary: The Seongsu branch of YOU Hair Salon (와이오유), a multi-branch chain built around a signature 15-step head spa alongside full-service cut and color.
you-hair-salon-seongsu.bestFor: a full 15-step head-spa scalp treatment paired with color, perm, or cut in one visit
you-hair-salon-seongsu.whyWeLikeIt: K-beauty head spa & hair clinic salon near Seongsu Station offering deep scalp cleansing, personalized hair care, and English-language service for visitors.
you-hair-salon-seongsu.longDescription:
YOU Hair Salon Seongsu (와이오유 성수) is the Seongsu branch of a multi-location Seoul chain — sister locations run in Pangyo and Bundang — a short walk from Seongsu Station. The offering centers on a 15-step head-spa treatment alongside standard cut, color, and perm services, aimed at handling scalp care and styling in the same visit.

The shop is foreigner-friendly, with English-speaking support and unhurried service noted by international visitors. Booking runs through Instagram DM (@yousalon_seongsu) a couple of days ahead, and the salon keeps hours of roughly 10am–6:30pm.

beauty-for-smile.name: Beauty for Smile
beauty-for-smile.summary: A Seongsu color specialist known for soft balayage and voluminous perm work using premium haircare lines.
beauty-for-smile.bestFor: soft, wearable balayage or a mellow perm from a colorist working exclusively in premium haircare lines
beauty-for-smile.whyWeLikeIt: Seongsu hair salon known for soft balayage/water-perm coloring using Davines and Shiseido haircare, with an optional head-spa add-on.
beauty-for-smile.longDescription:
Beauty for Smile (뷰티포스마일) is a color-focused hair salon on Yeonmujang 1-gil, open since 2020. The house style leans toward soft, wearable tones — ash brown, aqua beige — built through balayage and ombré techniques and finished with mellow or textured perms for volume and movement.

The salon works with premium haircare lines from Davines and Shiseido, and offers an optional head-spa add-on for scalp and hair conditioning after a color service. It keeps hours of 11am–8pm, closed Mondays, with booking through Instagram (@beautyforsmile_).

dior-cafe-seongsu-concept-store.name: Café Dior Seongsu
dior-cafe-seongsu-concept-store.summary: Dior's Seongsu concept-store café — a reservation-only garden café inside the brand's flagship, still running years past its original "temporary" window.
dior-cafe-seongsu-concept-store.bestFor: a splurge coffee inside a genuine luxury-flagship garden setting, if you can land a reservation
dior-cafe-seongsu-concept-store.whyWeLikeIt: Dior's Seongsu flagship, inspired by the Paris Montaigne store, pairs a French-garden setting with a premium café menu — a clean example of the luxury-brand-flagship-as-café trend.
dior-cafe-seongsu-concept-store.longDescription:
Café Dior Seongsu occupies the ground floor of Dior's Seongsu concept store on Yeonmujang 5-gil, a flagship inspired by the brand's Paris Montaigne store. It opened in May 2022 as a three-year temporary installation and has since been extended well past that original window, continuing to operate as of 2026.

The café serves a drinks-only menu inside a French-garden setting that changes with the seasons, seating only a handful of tables at a time. Seats are reservation-only through Dior's app, released monthly for the following month, though walk-in cancellations sometimes open up right at the 11am opening.

nudake-tea-house.name: NUDAKE Tea House
nudake-tea-house.summary: A tea-and-dessert concept bar on the fifth floor of Gentle Monster's Haus Nowhere flagship, built around visually striking tea sets and kinetic art.
nudake-tea-house.bestFor: a visually dramatic tea-and-dessert stop inside one of Seongsu's newest architectural flagships
nudake-tea-house.whyWeLikeIt: Occupies the striking 5th floor of Gentle Monster's "Haus Nowhere" concept store near Seoul Forest Station, cited as one of Seoul's most visually distinctive interior spaces.
nudake-tea-house.longDescription:
NUDAKE Tea House sits on the fifth floor of Haus Nowhere, Gentle Monster's flagship near Seoul Forest that opened in September 2025 as the first chapter of the brand's long-term retail vision. NUDAKE, Gentle Monster's dessert-and-tea offshoot, built the floor around a rotating collection of themed teas served in sculptural, sometimes claw-shaped ceramics.

Kinetic installations move through the space alongside a pistachio-and-violet color scheme, and the gift shop at the front sells tea by the cup from roughly 12,500 to 36,000 won. The tea lounge runs daily from around noon to 9pm; the adjoining gift shop opens earlier, at 11am.

texture-apgujeong-rodeo.name: Texture Apgujeong Rodeo
texture-apgujeong-rodeo.summary: A colour-focused hair salon on Apgujeong Rodeo, part of a small two-branch brand that treats dyeing and bond-repair as its signature.
texture-apgujeong-rodeo.bestFor: trend-led colour work and hair-repair treatments in the Apgujeong Rodeo shopping belt
texture-apgujeong-rodeo.whyWeLikeIt: It bills itself as a colour-and-wellness salon rather than a generic cut shop, and sits right on the Apgujeong Rodeo strip where the newest Seoul hair trends surface first.
texture-apgujeong-rodeo.longDescription:
Texture is a colour-specialist salon on the second floor of the YOHAN Building on Apgujeong-ro, at the heart of the Apgujeong Rodeo shopping district. It is one of two branches of the brand, alongside a Seoul Forest location, and frames itself as a "wellness salon" built around dyeing and clinic-style hair repair.

As a newly opened studio it books through its Instagram profile link, Naver reservations and DM. Hours run roughly 10:00 to 21:00, closed Wednesdays. Note that the brand's storefront and menu are Korean-first, so non-Korean speakers may want to book ahead with a translation app.

the-boutique-hauve-dosan.name: The Boutique Hauve Dosan
the-boutique-hauve-dosan.summary: A large, newly opened Apgujeong-Rodeo salon with around twenty chairs and a proprietary damaged-hair perm-and-treatment line.
the-boutique-hauve-dosan.bestFor: a spacious full-service cut, colour and perm session on the Apgujeong Rodeo strip
the-boutique-hauve-dosan.whyWeLikeIt: It opened in 2026 as a roomy ~90-pyeong salon with valet parking and its own "The Barrel" repair-perm line — an easy, comfortable full-service option in a premium neighbourhood.
the-boutique-hauve-dosan.longDescription:
The Boutique Hauve's Dosan branch is a large hair salon — roughly ninety pyeong with about twenty chairs — on the second floor at 312 Apgujeong-ro, on the Apgujeong Rodeo strip. It runs a proprietary "The Barrel" perm-and-treatment programme aimed at damaged hair, and offers valet parking.

As a 2026 opening it books through Instagram and Naver, and has run first-visit discount events. English service is limited, so booking ahead with a translation app is advisable.

typer-haus.name: Typer Haus
typer-haus.summary: A men's premium hair shop near Apgujeong Rodeo station, backed by a well-known men's-hair brand and branded entirely in English around the line "Type Your Persona."
typer-haus.bestFor: a men's cut and styling session in a design-forward Apgujeong studio
typer-haus.whyWeLikeIt: It's the new flagship-style offshoot of a major men's-hair brand, with strongly English-forward branding — an unusually approachable pick for male travellers wanting a Korean men's cut.
typer-haus.longDescription:
Typer Haus is a men's premium hair shop in the basement level at 20 Seolleung-ro 161-gil, a short walk from Apgujeong Rodeo station. It launched in mid-2026 as an offshoot of an established men's-hair brand with a large following, and leans into English branding — "MENS PREMIUM HAIR SHOP," "Type Your Persona."

Booking is by Instagram DM. As a men's-only studio its appeal is narrower, but the English-forward identity and prime location make it one of the easier men's salons for visitors to approach.

esyun-hair.name: ESYUN Hair Extensions
esyun-hair.summary: A hair-extension (붙임머리) specialist studio near Sinsa, with profile branding in Japanese as well as Korean.
esyun-hair.bestFor: adding length or volume with professional hair extensions
esyun-hair.whyWeLikeIt: It's a dedicated extension specialist rather than a general salon, and its Japanese-language profile signals it's used to serving Japanese-speaking visitors — a niche but genuinely tourist-friendly option.
esyun-hair.longDescription:
ESYUN is a hair-extension (붙임머리) specialist studio on the third floor at 45 Gangnam-daero 162-gil in Sinsa-dong, recently opened after relocating from Yongin. Its Instagram profile carries Korean and Japanese ("エクステ") branding, pointing to a Japanese-speaking clientele.

Booking is by Instagram DM or phone. This is a focused extensions studio rather than a full-service salon, so it suits travellers specifically after length or volume work.

the-gravel-cheongdam.name: The Gravel
the-gravel-cheongdam.summary: A high-end men's-only "gentlemen's hair lounge" in Cheongdam offering one-to-one private styling, scalp spa and hairpiece work.
the-gravel-cheongdam.bestFor: a private, unhurried men's cut, scalp-spa or styling session in Cheongdam
the-gravel-cheongdam.whyWeLikeIt: It's a 1:1 private atelier built around the idea of "designing your value" — a discreet, high-touch men's option in Seoul's most exclusive salon district.
the-gravel-cheongdam.longDescription:
The Gravel is a men's-only "gentlemen's hair lounge" on the third floor at 5 Dosan-daero 102-gil in Cheongdam. It works one-to-one in a private-atelier format, covering men's cutting and styling, scalp spa and hairpiece services, under a "Design Your Value" concept.

A 2026 opening, it books through Instagram. Content is largely Korean; the private format and Cheongdam address place it at the premium end of the men's-grooming market.

nailamuteun.name: Nailamuteun
nailamuteun.summary: A newly opened nail-art studio in Yeonnam-dong, tagging itself squarely to the Yeonnam and Hongdae nail scene.
nailamuteun.bestFor: on-trend Yeonnam nail art booked directly by DM
nailamuteun.whyWeLikeIt: It's exactly the rising, DM-booking Yeonnam nail studio our readers ask about — new, location-proud, and off the big booking platforms.
nailamuteun.longDescription:
Nailamuteun is a nail-art studio in a lower-level unit at 35 Seongmisan-ro 26-gil in Yeonnam-dong, the leafy neighbourhood just north of Hongdae. It opened in 2026 and identifies itself explicitly with the Yeonnam and Hongdae nail scene.

Booking is by Instagram DM. As a small independent studio it isn't listed on the big booking apps, which is precisely why it's worth surfacing for visitors who want a local Yeonnam nail session.

carp-nail.name: Carp Nail
carp-nail.summary: A small independent nail-art studio in Yeonnam-dong with a distinctive name and location-tagged Instagram.
carp-nail.bestFor: a Yeonnam nail-art appointment away from the chains
carp-nail.whyWeLikeIt: It's a genuinely independent Yeonnam studio — distinctive branding, DM booking, the kind of neighbourhood nail spot that rarely shows up in English guides.
carp-nail.longDescription:
Carp Nail is a nail-art studio on the second floor at 19 Donggyo-ro 32-gil in Yeonnam-dong. Newly licensed in 2026, it tags its work to Yeonnam and books directly through Instagram DM.

Small and off the major platforms, it suits travellers who prefer an independent neighbourhood studio over a chain.

orosyfuss-hapjeong-nail.name: The Prettier Nail & OROSYFUSS Hapjeong
orosyfuss-hapjeong-nail.summary: The Hapjeong branch of the OROSYFUSS group, combining nail art with problem-foot (문제성발) care in the Mapo Hangang Prugio complex.
orosyfuss-hapjeong-nail.bestFor: nail art plus specialist foot care near Hongdae/Hapjeong
orosyfuss-hapjeong-nail.whyWeLikeIt: It pairs standard nail art with genuine problem-foot care — a more clinical, useful combination than a typical nail bar, right by Hapjeong.
orosyfuss-hapjeong-nail.longDescription:
This is the Hapjeong branch of the OROSYFUSS group, on the ground floor of the Mapo Hangang Prugio commercial complex at 14 World Cup-ro 1-gil in Hapjeong-dong. It combines nail art with specialist problem-foot (문제성발) care.

Opened in 2026 with a live Naver booking link and Instagram DM, it sits within walking distance of the Hongdae/Hapjeong area.

jolly-nail-hapjeong.name: J.Olly Nail Art (Hapjeong)
jolly-nail-hapjeong.summary: A new Hapjeong-area branch of the multi-location Mapo K-beauty brand J.Olly, offering nail, lash and makeup together.
jolly-nail-hapjeong.bestFor: a one-stop nail, lash and makeup session near Hongdae
jolly-nail-hapjeong.whyWeLikeIt: It's a rising multi-service K-beauty brand — nails, lashes and makeup under one roof — expanding into the Hongdae/Seogyo area in 2026.
jolly-nail-hapjeong.longDescription:
J.Olly is a multi-location Mapo-gu K-beauty brand offering nails, lashes and makeup; this is its new Seogyo-dong (Hapjeong-area) branch on the second floor at 40 World Cup-ro. The flagship sits near Gongdeok.

Opened in 2026, it books through Instagram and Naver. The combined nail-lash-makeup menu makes it a convenient single stop for visitors near Hongdae.

hera-spa-esthetic.name: HERA Spa & Esthetic
hera-spa-esthetic.summary: A women-only hotel spa on the second floor of the Sejong Hotel by Myeongdong, offering scrub, facial, aroma and foot care.
hera-spa-esthetic.bestFor: a women-only hotel spa session — scrub, facial or aroma — steps from Myeongdong
hera-spa-esthetic.whyWeLikeIt: It's a proper hotel spa with its own page on the Sejong Hotel site, women-only and walkably close to Myeongdong — an easy, legible choice for visitors.
hera-spa-esthetic.longDescription:
HERA Spa & Esthetic is a women-only spa on the second floor of the Sejong Hotel at 145 Toegye-ro, beside Myeongdong. The hotel's own website lists it with a full menu of scrub, facial, aroma and foot-care treatments, hours of 09:30–22:00 and a direct phone line.

Being inside an established hotel makes it one of the more predictable, easy-to-book spa options for visitors staying around Myeongdong.

fleur-jardin-myeongdong.name: Fleur Jardin Myeongdong
fleur-jardin-myeongdong.summary: A Myeongdong skincare studio combining facials and skin analysis with nail and foot-spa services in the T Avenue building.
fleur-jardin-myeongdong.bestFor: a combined facial, skin-analysis and nail session in central Myeongdong
fleur-jardin-myeongdong.whyWeLikeIt: It bundles facials, skin analysis, nails and foot spa in one central Myeongdong address — convenient for visitors who want several beauty services in a single stop.
fleur-jardin-myeongdong.longDescription:
Fleur Jardin is a skincare studio on the second floor of the T Avenue building at 7-9 Myeongdong 10-gil in Myeongdong. Its menu spans facials and skin analysis alongside nail and foot-spa work.

The studio maintains an active Instagram and Naver blog and books through them; its central Myeongdong location makes it an easy add-on to a shopping day.

as-blanc-lotte-hotel-seoul.name: As Blanc (Lotte Hotel Seoul)
as-blanc-lotte-hotel-seoul.summary: A forthcoming branch of the As Blanc facial-spa brand on the seventh floor of Lotte Hotel Seoul, beside Myeongdong.
as-blanc-lotte-hotel-seoul.bestFor: a luxury hotel K-beauty facial by Myeongdong (opening late 2026)
as-blanc-lotte-hotel-seoul.whyWeLikeIt: As Blanc is a foreigner-ready K-beauty facial brand — English site, Klook listing, overseas branches — and this Lotte Hotel Seoul location will put it right beside Myeongdong.
as-blanc-lotte-hotel-seoul.longDescription:
As Blanc is a directly-managed K-beauty facial-spa brand that operates in luxury malls and hotels, with an English website, a Klook listing and an overseas branch. This location, on the seventh floor of Lotte Hotel Seoul at 30 Euljiro, is beside Myeongdong.

Note: the Lotte Hotel Seoul branch is slated to open around September 2026, so confirm it is operating before visiting.

cocorea-spa-myeongdong.name: COCOREA Spa (Myeongdong)
cocorea-spa-myeongdong.summary: The skincare-and-treatment arm of the COCOREA brand on Myeongdong 4-gil, focused on facials and modern skin devices.
cocorea-spa-myeongdong.bestFor: a device-led K-beauty facial in central Myeongdong
cocorea-spa-myeongdong.whyWeLikeIt: It's the facial/skin-treatment side of a multi-unit Myeongdong K-beauty brand — modern treatments like PDRN and skin devices, right on Myeongdong 4-gil.
cocorea-spa-myeongdong.longDescription:
COCOREA Spa is the skincare-and-treatment branch of the COCOREA brand, on the second floor at 17-1 Myeongdong 4-gil. It focuses on facials and current K-beauty skin treatments and devices. (Note the brand also runs a separate makeup and personal-colour unit nearby on the same street — this entry is the facial spa.)

A 2026 opening, it books through Instagram; its central Myeongdong position makes it a convenient skincare stop.

triomphe-esthetic.name: Triomphe Esthetic
triomphe-esthetic.summary: The esthetic arm of a Myeongdong medical-aesthetic clinic, with strong foreigner support including LINE, WeChat and WhatsApp booking.
triomphe-esthetic.bestFor: a clinic-grade esthetic facial in Myeongdong with multilingual booking
triomphe-esthetic.whyWeLikeIt: It's tied to a medical-aesthetic clinic and is unusually foreigner-ready — LINE, WeChat and WhatsApp contacts make it one of the easiest esthetic studios for visitors to book.
triomphe-esthetic.longDescription:
Triomphe Esthetic is the esthetic/skincare arm of Triomphe Dr. Clinic & Aesthetic, on the first floor of the Myeongdong Central Building at 16 Myeongdong 9-gil. It opened in late 2024 and runs its own booking line.

It stands out for foreigner readiness, offering LINE, WeChat and WhatsApp contacts alongside Naver — an easy pick for visitors who want a clinic-linked facial in central Myeongdong.

renk-euljiro.name: Re:NK Euljiro
renk-euljiro.summary: A Re:NK-brand facial spa inside the President Hotel near Euljiro-ipgu and Myeongdong.
renk-euljiro.bestFor: a Re:NK-brand facial near Euljiro-ipgu station
renk-euljiro.whyWeLikeIt: It's a named-brand facial spa inside a hotel by Euljiro-ipgu — a legible, centrally located option a short walk from Myeongdong.
renk-euljiro.longDescription:
Re:NK Euljiro is a facial and skincare spa run under the Re:NK brand, on the sixth floor (room 701) of the President Hotel at 16 Euljiro, near Euljiro-ipgu station and a short walk from Myeongdong.

The branch books through its KakaoTalk channel and Instagram DM. Content is Korean-first; the hotel setting and central location make it easy to find.

weneedblack-cheongdam.name: WENEEDBLACK The Cheongdam
weneedblack-cheongdam.summary: A newly opened Cheongdam hair salon under the WENEEDBLACK brand (operator LIVEX), with modern, trend-led cut and colour work.
weneedblack-cheongdam.bestFor: trend-led cut and colour in a premium Cheongdam salon
weneedblack-cheongdam.whyWeLikeIt: It's the Cheongdam branch of a brand with a growing following, opened in 2026 right in Seoul's most exclusive salon district.
weneedblack-cheongdam.longDescription:
WENEEDBLACK's Cheongdam branch sits on the third floor at 34 Apgujeong-ro 80-gil in Cheongdam-dong, run by the LIVEX group that also operates the premium WENEED flagship line. It opened in 2026 with modern, trend-focused hair work.

Booking is by DM on the brand's Instagram, which hosts this branch's content (there is no branch-only account). Content is largely Korean; the Cheongdam address places it at the premium end of the market.

signicho-nail-hongdae.name: Signicho Nail Hongdae
signicho-nail-hongdae.summary: A busy, budget-friendly nail-art studio on Hongdae's main walking street, with a heavy portfolio and a big following.
signicho-nail-hongdae.bestFor: affordable, photo-ready nail art right on the Hongdae walking street
signicho-nail-hongdae.whyWeLikeIt: It's exactly the rising Hongdae nail studio travellers ask about — a large active Instagram following, fixed budget-friendly pricing from around 29,000 won, and a central location on the walking street.
signicho-nail-hongdae.longDescription:
Signicho Nail is a nail-art studio on the second floor at 54 Eoulmadang-ro in Seogyo-dong, on Hongdae's main walking street. It runs a heavy nail-art portfolio, keeps fixed budget-friendly pricing (gel from around 29,000 won, monthly art from 39,000), and hours of 10:00–21:00, open year-round.

It books by Instagram DM and a Kakao channel. One of the more visible Hongdae nail studios among foreign visitors, it's a strong, easy pick.

sketch-on-nails.name: The Sketch Nails
sketch-on-nails.summary: A small Hongdae nail studio known for photogenic anime/character (오타쿠) nail art, minutes from Hongik University station.
sketch-on-nails.bestFor: highly photogenic character and anime-themed nail art near Hongdae station
sketch-on-nails.whyWeLikeIt: Its anime-and-character nail art is genuinely distinctive and internationally photogenic — a standout for visitors who want something beyond standard gel work.
sketch-on-nails.longDescription:
The Sketch Nails is a one-person nail studio on the lower level at 7 Wausan-ro 29na-gil in Seogyo-dong, a few minutes from Hongik University station exit 7. It specialises in photogenic anime and character (오타쿠) nail art, with fixed monthly-art pricing around 39,000 won.

Its profile carries Japanese as well as Korean, and it books through Naver reservation and Instagram DM. As a small independent shop it isn't on the big platforms — part of its appeal.

gonggan-nail-hongdae.name: Gonggan Nail (Hongdae Branch 2)
gonggan-nail-hongdae.summary: The second Hongdae branch of the established Gonggan Nail chain, in the LG Palace building by Hongik University station.
gonggan-nail-hongdae.bestFor: reliable chain-quality gel and nail art near Hongdae station
gonggan-nail-hongdae.whyWeLikeIt: It's a branch of a well-run nail-art chain — gel, extensions and monthly art with dependable quality — a lower-risk option than an unknown independent.
gonggan-nail-hongdae.longDescription:
Gonggan Nail's second Hongdae branch is on the fifth floor (room 605) of the LG Palace building at 156 Yanghwa-ro in Donggyo-dong, by Hongik University station. It opened in 2026 as part of an established Seoul nail-art chain covering gel, extensions and monthly art, with hours of 10:00–21:00.

Booking is via Naver and DM. Note this specific branch has no dedicated Instagram — reach it through the brand's official account and website, quoting the 156 Yanghwa-ro, room 605 address so you land at the right location.

hikari-skin-massage.name: Hikari Skin Massage
hikari-skin-massage.summary: A long-running Myeongdong skin-and-body massage shop geared to Japanese-speaking visitors, near Myeongdong station.
hikari-skin-massage.bestFor: skin and body massage in Myeongdong with Japanese-language service
hikari-skin-massage.whyWeLikeIt: It has served Myeongdong since around 2020 with Japanese-speaking staff and LINE booking — an easy, established choice for Japanese-speaking travellers.
hikari-skin-massage.longDescription:
Hikari is a skin-and-body massage shop on the fifth floor at 18 Myeongdong 8na-gil in Chungmuro 1-ga, near Myeongdong station exit 6. It has operated in Myeongdong since around 2020 and re-registered at this location, and is strongly oriented to Japanese-speaking visitors, with Japanese captions and LINE booking.

It books by LINE, phone and the heally platform. Services skew toward massage and skin/body care; English support is limited, so Japanese speakers will find it easiest.

n-seoul-tower.name: N Seoul Tower
n-seoul-tower.summary: Seoul's landmark tower on Namsan — the city's default first view, and its most photographed one after dark.
n-seoul-tower.bestFor: a first orientation to the city
n-seoul-tower.whyWeLikeIt: Nearly ten thousand ratings hold it at 4.2 — unusual consistency for a landmark that sees this much traffic, and a fair signal that the view delivers on the climb.
n-seoul-tower.longDescription:
N Seoul Tower stands at the summit of Namsan, in Yongsan-gu, and functions as the city's orientation point: the observation deck gives you the whole basin at once, which is the fastest way to understand how Seoul is laid out before you start walking it.

The tower is busiest after sunset, when the night view is the draw. Its rating sits at 4.2 across more than 9,600 ratings — a large enough sample that the number means something. Getting up is part of the visit; the cable car from Myeongdong is the usual route, and the walk up through Namsan Park is the quieter one.

Namdaemun Market sits at the foot of the hill, close enough to pair the two in an afternoon.

lotte-world-tower-mall.name: Lotte World Tower & Mall
lotte-world-tower-mall.summary: Seoul's tallest building — a 555-meter Jamsil complex holding a mall, hotel, and cinema, with the Seoul Sky observatory as just one part of it.
lotte-world-tower-mall.bestFor: a full afternoon of shopping and dining anchored by one landmark tower
lotte-world-tower-mall.whyWeLikeIt: At 555 meters, it was among the world's five tallest buildings when it opened in 2017 — worth knowing before deciding whether to also pay for the Seoul Sky ticket inside it.
lotte-world-tower-mall.longDescription:
Lotte World Tower & Mall is the 555-meter skyscraper complex that anchors Jamsil, in Songpa-gu — 123 floors that ranked among the world's five tallest buildings on its 2017 opening. The tower holds the Signiel hotel and, on floors 117 to 123, the Seoul Sky observation deck, covered separately in this guide.

At street level the complex spreads into a shopping mall, a cinema, a concert hall, and a run of restaurants — enough to fill an afternoon before anyone goes near the observatory. Its rating sits at 4.4 across roughly 900 reviews, reflecting the mall and hotel experience as much as the tower itself.

It sits directly on Jamsil Station (lines 2 and 8), with the mall entrance built into the transit hub.

seoul-sky.name: Seoul Sky
seoul-sky.summary: The observation deck on floors 117–123 of Lotte World Tower — the highest vantage point in Seoul, with a glass floor underfoot.
seoul-sky.bestFor: the highest view over Seoul, glass floor included
seoul-sky.whyWeLikeIt: It's the specific reason to go up the tower — the glass-floor section and the open-air Sky Terrace exist only at this level, separate from anything the mall below offers.
seoul-sky.longDescription:
Seoul Sky occupies the top seven floors of Lotte World Tower — 117 through 123 — putting its observation floors between 472 and 498 meters above ground, the highest public vantage point in the city. The visit takes in a standard indoor observation floor, a glass-floored section that puts you directly over the drop, and an open-air Sky Terrace near the very top.

It shares its address and building with Lotte World Tower & Mall, but it is a separate, separately ticketed attraction — the tower's shopping, dining, and hotel floors are a different visit, covered elsewhere in this guide. Seoul Sky holds a 4.3 rating across roughly 300 reviews.

Tickets are sold at a dedicated entrance inside the mall in Jamsil, and the elevator ride up is part of the experience.

seoul-city-wall.name: Seoul City Wall
seoul-city-wall.summary: Hanyangdoseong, the 18.6-kilometer Joseon-era fortress wall that still traces four of Seoul's inner mountains — a walking route as much as a monument.
seoul-city-wall.bestFor: a self-guided heritage walk with skyline views built into the route
seoul-city-wall.whyWeLikeIt: It's on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list, and unlike most fortress walls this old, long stretches of it are still open to walk rather than roped off.
seoul-city-wall.longDescription:
Seoul City Wall — Hanyangdoseong — was first built in 1396 to enclose the new Joseon capital and runs 18.6 kilometers along the ridgelines of Baegaksan, Naksan, Namsan, and Inwangsan. Rather than one site, it's a network of walking courses: the Baegak course (Changuimun to Hyehwamun) and the Naksan course (Hyehwamun to Heunginjimun) are the two most associated with Jongno-gu, passing the Hanyangdoseong Museum and Naksan Park.

The wall links Seoul's historic great and minor gates, and stretches along Naksan and Namsan open onto unobstructed views back over the city center — the Namsan course leads directly toward N Seoul Tower. It's on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list.

There's no single entrance; access is trailhead by trailhead, and the city's official Hanyangdoseong site maps every course and gate.

jeongdong-observatory.name: Jeongdong Observatory
jeongdong-observatory.summary: A free public viewpoint on the 13th floor of Seoul City Hall's Seosomun annex, looking straight down over Deoksugung Palace.
jeongdong-observatory.bestFor: a free, quiet view over Deoksugung without a ticket or a queue
jeongdong-observatory.whyWeLikeIt: It holds a 4.4 average across a modest 37 ratings — a small but consistent number for a spot many visitors don't know to look for.
jeongdong-observatory.longDescription:
Jeongdong Observatory sits on the 13th floor of Seoul City Hall's Seosomun annex building in Jung-gu, looking directly down over Deoksugung Palace and the Jeongdong neighborhood around it. It opened in 2013, closed for a period afterward, and has since reopened with expanded hours: weekdays 13:30–17:30 and weekends 9:00–17:30, closed on most public holidays. Admission is free, and there's a small café on the same floor.

As of mid-2026, Seoul City Hall also runs a second, newer observation floor in its main building nearby — a separate facility with its own entrance, not to be confused with this one. Both are free and city-run, but Jeongdong Observatory is the older, quieter of the two, and the one with the Deoksugung view.

gimpo-intl-airport-observatory-deck.name: Gimpo Int'l Airport Observatory Deck
gimpo-intl-airport-observatory-deck.summary: An outdoor deck on the domestic terminal's 4th floor at Gimpo International Airport, close enough to watch aircraft taxi and take off.
gimpo-intl-airport-observatory-deck.bestFor: watching domestic flights up close before or after a trip
gimpo-intl-airport-observatory-deck.longDescription:
Gimpo International Airport's observatory deck sits at the far end of the 4th floor of the domestic passenger terminal, reachable straight from the terminal's food court. It opened in October 2018 as part of the domestic terminal's remodeling, and it's an open-air deck separated from the apron by wire fencing rather than glass — close enough to watch aircraft push back, taxi, and take off.

Because it sits on the domestic side, only domestic flights are visible; the international terminal is on the opposite side of the airport grounds and out of view from here. The rating is modest, 3.5 across 20 ratings, in keeping with a bare-bones facility rather than a dedicated attraction — a free bonus for travelers already at the airport more than a destination on its own.

A different, no-longer-public viewing room elsewhere in the airport complex has a similar history; this is the domestic-terminal deck, still open to anyone passing through.

cultural-complex-j-bug.name: Cultural Complex J-Bug
cultural-complex-j-bug.summary: A caterpillar-shaped cultural complex inside Ttukseom Hangang Park — officially Seoul Saenggak-maru — with a library, café, and river-facing views.
cultural-complex-j-bug.serviceDetail: Riverside cultural complex — library, café & exhibits
cultural-complex-j-bug.bestFor: a quiet library-and-river break inside Ttukseom Hangang Park
cultural-complex-j-bug.whyWeLikeIt: The building itself is the hook — a 243-meter structure shaped like an inchworm, which is where the nickname "J-Bug" comes from.
cultural-complex-j-bug.longDescription:
Cultural Complex J-Bug is the popular nickname for Seoul Saenggak-maru, a 243-meter, caterpillar-shaped building inside Ttukseom Hangang Park in Gwangjin-gu. Inside are a public library, meeting rooms, a café, and a small exhibition hall on the Han River's history — a low-key alternative to the park's open lawns when the weather doesn't cooperate.

Upper floors and the building's river-facing side give views up and down the Han, though the site is built for lingering rather than for the view alone. It's closed on Mondays and on New Year's Day, Lunar New Year, and Chuseok.

The nearest access point is Jayang Station (Line 7), Ttukseom Hangang Park exit, about a ten-minute walk into the park.

63-skypicnic.name: 63 Skypicnic
63-skypicnic.summary: A newly reopened art-and-media observatory on the 60th and 63rd floors of Yeouido's 63 Building.
63-skypicnic.bestFor: a media-art take on the classic high-rise view, plus a rooftop rarely open to the public
63-skypicnic.whyWeLikeIt: The 63rd-floor rooftop had been closed to visitors for years over safety concerns; its reopening as part of 63 Skypicnic in June 2026 is the news here.
63-skypicnic.longDescription:
63 Skypicnic is the observation deck that opened inside Yeouido's 63 Building on June 4, 2026, replacing the tower's earlier observatory. The main level, on the 60th floor, combines a media-art installation with mirrored surfaces and projection screens, an immersive screening room, a café, and a gift shop rather than a plain viewing platform.

The draw beyond the art is the 63rd-floor rooftop, which reopened here after years of closure over safety concerns — one of the few genuinely open-air rooftops among Seoul's tall-building observatories, and the best of the three levels for watching the Han River move from sunset into night.

Tickets are sold from the ground floor, with the observatory itself starting at the 60th.

riverview-8th-avenue.name: Riverview 8th Avenue
riverview-8th-avenue.summary: A glass-floored viewing platform built into a pier of Gwangjin Bridge — one of only three bridge-pier observatories in the world.
riverview-8th-avenue.bestFor: a free, glass-floor view of the Han River built into a bridge pier
riverview-8th-avenue.whyWeLikeIt: It's one of only three observatories of its kind anywhere, alongside comparable decks on Paris's Bir-Hakeim Bridge and Tokyo's Rainbow Bridge — and visitor numbers back its growing reputation: the city's own count went from roughly 15,000 in 2023 to over 107,000 in 2025.
riverview-8th-avenue.longDescription:
Riverview 8th Avenue sits beneath the eighth pier of Gwangjin Bridge, on the Gangdong-gu bank of the Han River. A glass floor lets visitors look straight down at the water, and the enclosed, glass-walled space frames both directions of the river along with the skylines of Gwangjin-gu and Gangdong-gu. It's one of only three bridge-pier observatories in the world.

The space also hosts small exhibitions and occasional talks. It's a seasonal facility, open only March through November and closed entirely from December through February; hours run noon to 6 p.m. in March and November and noon to 8 p.m. from April through October, and it's also closed on Mondays, Lunar New Year, and Chuseok. Admission is free.

It's about a 15-minute walk from either Gwangnaru or Cheonho station on Line 5.

chaeseokjang-observatory.name: Chaeseokjang Observatory
chaeseokjang-observatory.summary: A rooftop viewpoint built atop a former Japanese colonial-era quarry cliff in Changsin-dong, with a café built into the level below.
chaeseokjang-observatory.bestFor: an off-the-tourist-track skyline view with real neighborhood history behind it
chaeseokjang-observatory.whyWeLikeIt: The quarry it sits on supplied granite for colonial-era landmark buildings — a piece of Seoul's history most skyline views don't come with.
chaeseokjang-observatory.longDescription:
Chaeseokjang Observatory — also known as the Changsin-Sungin Quarry Observatory — sits atop a former granite quarry cliff in Changsin-dong, Jongno-gu. The quarry was cut into Naksan's hillside during the Japanese colonial period to supply stone for buildings including the old Government-General building and the Bank of Korea; after the war, displaced families settled the quarry site into the hillside village that still surrounds the observatory today.

The building opened in 2019: a glass-walled second floor holds Café Nakta, and the rooftop above it is an open, unobstructed platform over the quarry cliff and the Seoul skyline beyond. It's closed on Mondays.

It's about an 11-minute walk from Changsin Station (Line 6), inside the same hillside neighborhood as Naksan Park.

eungbongsan-palgakjeong.name: Eungbongsan Palgakjeong
eungbongsan-palgakjeong.summary: A traditional octagonal pavilion at the summit of Eungbongsan — one of Seoul's classic Han River night-view spots, reached by a short hike.
eungbongsan-palgakjeong.bestFor: a short hike to one of Seoul's classic night-view spots
eungbongsan-palgakjeong.whyWeLikeIt: The mountain served as a royal hunting ground in the Joseon dynasty, and the eight-sided pavilion at its summit is a small, quiet payoff for what's only about a 30-minute climb.
eungbongsan-palgakjeong.longDescription:
Eungbongsan Palgakjeong is the octagonal pavilion at the 94-meter summit of Eungbongsan, in Seongdong-gu, near where the Han River meets Jungnangcheon stream. A wooden staircase path climbs from the base to the pavilion in around 30 minutes, passing benches and exercise equipment along the way; the mountain itself served as a royal hunting ground during the Joseon dynasty.

From the pavilion, the view takes in the Han River, Apgujeong across the water, and — on clear days — Lotte World Tower and the mountains beyond, which is what has made it one of Seoul's regularly recommended night-view spots.

The nearest stop is Eungbong Station on the Gyeongui-Jungang Line, about a ten-minute walk to the trailhead.

namdaemun-market.name: Namdaemun Market
namdaemun-market.summary: Korea's largest traditional market, next to Sungnyemun Gate — clothing, housewares, and ginseng across about 20,000 wholesale and retail shops.
namdaemun-market.bestFor: browsing Korea's largest general market, from clothing to ginseng
namdaemun-market.whyWeLikeIt: The wholesale side keeps overnight hours — 11pm to 4am — when retailers from around the country come in to buy.
namdaemun-market.longDescription:
Namdaemun Market sits just north of Sungnyemun Gate in Jung-gu, and carries roughly 600 years of history by the city's own count. It's Korea's largest traditional market, with about 20,000 wholesale and retail shops spread across the site.

The market deals in general merchandise rather than one specialty: clothing, eyewear, kitchenware, toys, mountain and fishing gear, stationery, hats, carpets, flowers, and ginseng all have their own stall clusters, alongside an imported-goods section. Daytime hours vary from store to store, and the wholesale side trades overnight, from 11pm to 4am.

It's a short walk from Myeongdong and from Namsan, making it easy to fold into a walk that also takes in N Seoul Tower.

kwangjang-market.name: Kwangjang Market
kwangjang-market.summary: Korea's first permanent private market, opened in 1905 — a food alley of bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and yukhoe, alongside a second-floor fabric wholesale trade.
kwangjang-market.bestFor: trying market-stall bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and yukhoe in one alley
kwangjang-market.whyWeLikeIt: It opened in 1905 as Korea's first permanent, privately funded market, and its second-floor fabric wholesale section still runs over 100 meters of stalls.
kwangjang-market.longDescription:
Kwangjang Market opened in 1905 in Jongno-gu, built with private Korean capital at a time when most markets were temporary, days-long affairs — making it the country's first market designed to operate every day, permanently. Its name comes from the two bridges, Gwanggyo and Janggyo, that once stood at either end of the site.

The market's food alley sells mung bean pancakes (bindaetteok), soy-and-mustard-dressed mini rolls known as mayak gimbap, and raw beef tartare (yukhoe) from stalls packed close together, most open from early morning into the evening. A second-floor fabric wholesale market runs alongside it, with stalls selling bolts of cloth.

It's reachable on foot from either Jongno 5-ga Station (Line 1) or Euljiro 4-ga Station (Lines 2 and 5).

ssamzigil.name: Ssamzigil
ssamzigil.summary: A four-floor craft-shopping complex in Insadong, built around a spiral ramp that lets you walk the whole building without stairs.
ssamzigil.bestFor: craft shopping and a hands-on workshop class in Insadong
ssamzigil.whyWeLikeIt: The spiral ramp was built so you can walk all four floors without a single staircase — the layout is as much the point as what's sold inside it.
ssamzigil.longDescription:
Ssamzigil opened in 2004 on Insadong-gil in Jongno-gu, built around a continuous spiral ramp that winds up through four above-ground floors without a staircase anywhere in the building. More than 70 craft shops line the ramp, selling ceramics, jewelry, stationery, and other handmade goods.

The basement floor holds an experience workshop where visitors can book same-day classes in pottery painting, mother-of-pearl inlay, leatherwork, glasswork, or soap-making. A ground-floor courtyard hosts rotating performances and exhibitions, and a rooftop garden sits above the top floor.

Ssamzigil is a short walk from Anguk Station (Line 3, Exit 6), in the middle of the wider Insadong shopping street.

noryangjin-fisheries-wholesale-market.name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
noryangjin-fisheries-wholesale-market.summary: Seoul's largest wholesale fish market, run by Suhyup — buy from the tanks on the trading floor, then have it prepared at one of the restaurants upstairs.
noryangjin-fisheries-wholesale-market.bestFor: picking your own live seafood on the trading floor and eating it upstairs
noryangjin-fisheries-wholesale-market.whyWeLikeIt: Auctions start in the middle of the night — shellfish from around 1am, live fish from 3am — so the floor is already trading hours before most of the city is up.
noryangjin-fisheries-wholesale-market.longDescription:
Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market, in Dongjak-gu, is Seoul's largest consumer-facing fish market, operated by Suhyup Noryangjin Fisheries Co. The trading floor works on a section-by-section schedule: shellfish auctions from about 1am, premium fresh fish from 1:30am, live fish from 3am, with retail sales continuing through the day.

You can buy raw fish, shellfish, or other seafood directly from a tank-front vendor on the ground floor, then carry it upstairs to one of the market's restaurants to have it sliced and served, paying only a preparation fee. The market closes on Sundays, January 1st, and the Lunar New Year and Chuseok holidays.

It's next to Noryangjin Station, on Lines 1 and 9.

majang-meat-market.name: Majang Meat Market
majang-meat-market.summary: Korea's largest meat wholesale market, in Seongdong-gu — around 1,500 stalls trading hanwoo and other cuts, many of which will grill what you buy on the spot.
majang-meat-market.bestFor: buying hanwoo beef at wholesale stalls and having it grilled on the spot
majang-meat-market.whyWeLikeIt: It handles an estimated 60 to 70% of livestock distribution across the greater Seoul area, with around 2 million visitors passing through its roughly 1,500 stalls each year.
majang-meat-market.longDescription:
Majang Meat Market, sometimes called Majang-dong Livestock Market, is Korea's largest meat wholesale market, with roughly 1,500 vendors trading in Seongdong-gu. Livestock is processed and distributed through the market on an hourly basis, and the district's own count puts its share of livestock distribution across the greater Seoul area at 60 to 70%.

Hanwoo — Korean native-breed beef — is the market's signature product, sold directly from wholesale butchers rather than a retail counter. Many stalls will sell you a cut and point you to an adjoining grill room to cook and eat it immediately. General hours run from 3am to 11pm, with the market closed on the first and third Sunday of each month.

It's about a 10-minute walk from either Yongdu Station (Line 2) or Majang Station (Line 5).

jungbu-market.name: Jungbu Market
jungbu-market.summary: A wholesale dried-seafood market in Euljiro — laver, seaweed, anchovies, squid, and pollack, sold by the box and in smaller retail quantities.
jungbu-market.bestFor: stocking up on dried seafood and Korean pantry staples by the box
jungbu-market.longDescription:
Jungbu Market, in Jung-gu's Euljiro neighborhood, specializes in dried seafood: laver and other seaweed, dried anchovies, yellow corvina, squid, pollack, and filefish fillets, sold both wholesale and retail. Ginseng is also sold alongside the seafood at a number of stores.

The market keeps wholesale hours, opening as early as 3 or 4am and largely closing by late afternoon, with stores shut on Sundays.

It's about a two-minute walk from Euljiro 4-ga Station, on Lines 2 and 5.

mangwon-market.name: Mangwon Market
mangwon-market.summary: A neighborhood market in Mapo-gu selling fruit, vegetables, seafood, and street-food snacks, close to both Mangnidan-gil and Hangang Park.
mangwon-market.bestFor: a produce-and-food-stall neighborhood market next to Mangnidan-gil
mangwon-market.longDescription:
Mangwon Market is a neighborhood market in Mangwon-dong, Mapo-gu, selling fruit, vegetables, seafood, and manufactured goods, alongside stalls of prepared food — deep-fried and braised chicken, jokbal, and battered green chili peppers among them.
