It sits close to both Mangnidan-gil and Hangang Park, which makes it easy to fold into a walk through either. Stores keep their own hours and days off, generally closing around 9pm.

It's a short walk from Mangwon Station, on Line 6.

garak-market.name: Garak Market
garak-market.summary: Korea's first public wholesale market for produce and seafood when it opened in 1985, and now the country's largest — fruit, vegetables, and fisheries products traded at wholesale in Songpa-gu.
garak-market.bestFor: seeing the scale of Korea's largest wholesale produce and seafood market
garak-market.whyWeLikeIt: Around 7,300 tons of goods move through the market on a normal trading day.
garak-market.longDescription:
Garak Market opened in June 1985 in Songpa-gu as Korea's first public wholesale market for agricultural and marine products, and is now the largest in the country, on a site of 542,920 square meters. It trades fruit, vegetables, and fisheries products.

Wholesale trading runs overnight — the floor is already working at 2am, when most of the city is asleep.

It's beside Garak Market Station, on Lines 3 and 8.

seoul-folk-flea-market.name: Seoul Folk Flea Market
seoul-folk-flea-market.summary: An indoor flea market in seven color-coded buildings in Dongdaemun-gu — antiques, secondhand clothing, and household curios across nearly 900 shops.
seoul-folk-flea-market.bestFor: digging through antiques and secondhand goods in one indoor market
seoul-folk-flea-market.whyWeLikeIt: The market's seven buildings are each color-coded to a shade of the rainbow — a system that makes an 894-shop complex easier to navigate than it sounds.
seoul-folk-flea-market.longDescription:
Seoul Folk Flea Market — officially Seoul Pungmul Market — relocated to its current site near Sinseol-dong, where it now occupies seven buildings, each assigned one color of the rainbow, holding around 894 shops. It was named a Seoul Future Heritage site in 2015.

The market deals mostly in secondhand and antique goods: old furniture, clocks, cameras, records, tools, and vintage clothing are its core categories, with one building given over largely to antiques and handicrafts. Shop hours run 10am to 7pm, with the market's food court staying open until 10pm; the whole market closes on Tuesdays.

It's a short walk from Sinseol-dong Station, Exit 9, on Lines 1 and 2.

dongmyo-flea-market.name: Dongmyo Flea Market
dongmyo-flea-market.summary: An open-air secondhand market along the stone walls of Dongmyo Park, where merchants have gathered since the 1980s — vintage clothing and shoes are its biggest category now.
dongmyo-flea-market.bestFor: sorting through streetside racks of secondhand and vintage clothing
dongmyo-flea-market.whyWeLikeIt: In the market's clothing piles, pieces commonly go for ₩1,000 to ₩5,000.
dongmyo-flea-market.longDescription:
Dongmyo Flea Market runs along the stone walls of Dongmyo Park in Jongno-gu, where merchants began gathering to sell secondhand goods in the 1980s. It has since grown into one of Seoul's largest flea markets, with about 600 stalls along the walls and the side streets near Dongmyo Station.

Antiques are the base trade — rotary dial phones and old television sets, film posters, rare books, wallets — though vintage clothing and shoes have become the biggest category. Food stalls sell bindaetteok and boiled duck eggs among the goods. Stalls open daily from about 10am to 6pm, with hours varying by store.

It's about 60 meters from Exit 3 of Dongmyo Station, on Lines 1 and 6.

mapo-agricultural-marine-products-market.name: Mapo Agricultural & Marine Products Market
mapo-agricultural-marine-products-market.summary: A two-story seafood and produce market near Seoul World Cup Stadium — shops on the ground floor, sashimi centers and restaurants upstairs.
mapo-agricultural-marine-products-market.bestFor: buying fresh seafood near World Cup Stadium and having it prepared upstairs
mapo-agricultural-marine-products-market.longDescription:
Mapo Agricultural and Marine Products Market opened in 1998 near Seoul World Cup Stadium in Mapo-gu's Seongsan-dong, and is managed and run by the Mapo-gu Facilities Management Corporation. It's a two-story standalone building: the ground floor holds shops selling seafood, fruit, and vegetables, plus a supermarket, and the second floor is given over to sashimi centers and restaurants.

Seafood bought downstairs can be carried up to be sliced and served on the floor above. The market has its own parking lot.

It's near World Cup Stadium Station, on Line 6.

gongdeok-market.name: Gongdeok Market
gongdeok-market.summary: A neighborhood market on Mallijae-ro in Mapo-gu, home to Jokbal Alley — a row of braised pig's-trotter restaurants — and, next to it, a Jeon Alley of Korean savory pancakes.
gongdeok-market.bestFor: jokbal — braised pig's trotters — in Gongdeok's Jokbal Alley
gongdeok-market.whyWeLikeIt: Jokbal Alley formed around 30 years ago, after one restaurant's success drew others to open nearby; many of its stores have now been in place for more than 30 years.
gongdeok-market.longDescription:
Gongdeok Market is on Mallijae-ro in Mapo-gu, about 130 meters from Exit 5 of Gongdeok Station. Jokbal Alley, inside the market, is a row of restaurants serving jokbal — pork trotters braised in soy sauce and spices — usually with sundae (Korean blood sausage) and sundaeguk, the soup made from it. Next to it, Jeon Alley has eateries serving jeon, Korean savory pancakes, lined up on either side of the lane.

Gongdeok Station is served by Lines 5 and 6, the Gyeongui–Jungang Line, and the Airport Railroad.

jongno-3-ga-stalls-alley.name: Jongno 3-ga Stalls Alley
jongno-3-ga-stalls-alley.summary: A stretch of orange-tented pojangmacha food carts near Jongno 3-ga Station that sets up after dark — seafood, tteokbokki, and fried snacks eaten standing at plastic tables.
jongno-3-ga-stalls-alley.bestFor: an evening of pojangmacha-style street food and drinks
jongno-3-ga-stalls-alley.longDescription:
Jongno 3-ga's stalls alley is a stretch of pojangmacha — orange-tented street food carts — that sets up along the sidewalk near Exits 5 and 6 of Jongno 3-ga Station once the sun goes down.

Menus vary cart to cart but lean toward tteokbokki, sundae stir-fry, tempura, kimchi pancakes, and grilled or raw seafood, eaten standing or seated at plastic tables and stools set up on the pavement. Carts typically open in the early evening and stay open late into the night.

The alley doesn't have a single street address — it's an informal cluster of vendors rather than one building — but it's easy to find by walking out of Jongno 3-ga Station (Lines 1, 3, and 5) toward Exits 5 or 6 after dark.

yeongdeungpo-market.name: Yeongdeungpo Market
yeongdeungpo-market.summary: An old neighborhood market in Yeongdeungpo-gu, with a lane of sundae (blood sausage) shops facing each other from both sides.
yeongdeungpo-market.bestFor: sundaeguk — blood sausage soup — in the market's sundae alley
yeongdeungpo-market.longDescription:
Yeongdeungpo Market has operated in Yeongdeungpo-gu since around the end of Japanese colonial rule. Around 600 merchants trade there across 311 shops and 388 street stalls, selling manufactured goods, groceries, produce and seafood, dried fish, meat, and clothing.

One lane of the market is a sundae alley, where shops selling sundae (Korean blood sausage) and sundaeguk (blood sausage soup) face each other from both sides — one of them has been trading since 1966. Sundae is boiled in the afternoon, so that's the better half of the day to come if you want to take some away.

It's next to Yeongdeungpo Market Station, Exit 3, on Line 5.

shinheung-market.name: Shinheung Market
shinheung-market.summary: A 1950s covered market in Haebangchon, at the foot of Namsan, now home to independent bookstores, vintage shops, and cafés under a new transparent roof.
shinheung-market.bestFor: café-hopping through a converted 1950s market arcade in Haebangchon
shinheung-market.whyWeLikeIt: The market's aging arcade roof was torn out and replaced with a clear cover, so the covered alley now lets in daylight whatever the weather.
shinheung-market.longDescription:
Shinheung Market was established in 1953 in Haebangchon, on a slope at the foot of Namsan in Yongsan-gu. It operated for decades as a conventional neighborhood market before its old, aging arcade roof was removed and replaced with a transparent cover, letting daylight into the covered alley regardless of weather.

Independent businesses have moved into much of the market since — bookstores, vintage and secondhand shops, and small cafés now occupy space once held by grocery and household-goods vendors, alongside a few longer-running food stalls. The alley is narrow and sloped, with old signage still hanging over new storefronts.

It's within walking distance of Noksapyeong Station, on Line 6.

gongneungdong-goblin-market.name: Gongneungdong Goblin Market
gongneungdong-goblin-market.summary: A neighborhood market in Nowon-gu at the end of the Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail, tracing back to vendors who gathered by the old Gyeongchun railway line.
gongneungdong-goblin-market.bestFor: a market stop at the end of a Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail walk
gongneungdong-goblin-market.whyWeLikeIt: Its name comes from the vendors' habit of scattering at the sign of a crackdown and reassembling along the tracks — there and gone like a goblin.
gongneungdong-goblin-market.longDescription:
Gongneungdong Goblin Market traces back to street vendors who gathered near what's now Hwarangdae Station after the Gyeongchun railway line opened on July 25, 1939. It's a covered, arcade-style market today, selling meat and produce, groceries, and miscellaneous goods, with restaurants mixed in.

It sits at the end of the Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail, the walking-and-cycling path built on the old railway's former route. Since around 2019, the market has developed alongside that trail into more of a destination stop.

It's near Taereung Entrance Station, on Lines 6 and 7.

yeongcheon-market.name: Yeongcheon Market
yeongcheon-market.summary: A covered market in Seodaemun-gu, by Dongnimmun (Independence Gate) — once one of Seoul's largest wholesale rice-cake markets.
yeongcheon-market.bestFor: a covered neighborhood market by Independence Gate
yeongcheon-market.whyWeLikeIt: Kkwabaegi — twisted doughnuts — are enough of a fixture here that more than ten shops were selling them in the market in the 1970s.
yeongcheon-market.longDescription:
Yeongcheon Market formed in the 1960s near Dongnimmun (Independence Gate) in Seodaemun-gu, starting as a tteok (rice cake) alley near the old Seodaemun Prison, and for a stretch of its history was one of Seoul's largest wholesale markets for rice cakes. It runs under an arcade roof today, selling kkwabaegi (twisted doughnuts), tteokbokki, meat, fish, vegetables, and fruit.

Its northern entrance faces Dongnimmun, and the market is next to Dongnimmun Station on Line 3. Seodaemun Station, on Line 5, is about 500 meters away by Exit 2.

myeongdong-night-market.name: Myeongdong Night Market
myeongdong-night-market.summary: Myeongdong's nightly street-food corridor — stalls set up along Myeongdong-gil and its side streets each evening, running roughly from dusk to around midnight.
myeongdong-night-market.bestFor: an evening of Myeongdong's street food once the daytime shops close
myeongdong-night-market.longDescription:
Myeongdong Night Market is the name commonly given to the street-food scene that takes over Myeongdong-gil and its side streets each evening, once the neighborhood's daytime fashion and cosmetics shops start winding down. Vendors typically begin setting up carts in the late afternoon.

Skewers of grilled meat, hotteok (a filled, pan-fried sweet pancake), tteokbokki, grilled and battered seafood, and baked cheese dishes are the mainstays, sold from carts concentrated within a few minutes' walk of Myeongdong Station. Unlike Namdaemun or Gwangjang, it isn't organized around a single market building — it's an evening layer on top of Myeongdong's regular shopping street, and it packs up again by around midnight.

It's centered on Myeongdong Station, Exit 6, on Line 4.

starfield-coex-mall.name: Starfield COEX Mall
starfield-coex-mall.summary: The underground mall beneath the COEX complex in Samseong-dong, holding an aquarium, a multiplex and a free public library.
starfield-coex-mall.bestFor: a long indoor afternoon that mixes shopping with an aquarium and a library
starfield-coex-mall.whyWeLikeIt: It holds a 4.0 rating across more than 900 ratings — a large enough sample for the number to mean something.
starfield-coex-mall.longDescription:
Starfield COEX Mall runs beneath the COEX complex at 513 Yeongdong-daero, in Samseong-dong. Alongside the shops it holds the COEX Aquarium, a Megabox multiplex and the Starfield Library.

The library occupies two levels at the middle of the mall — 2,800 square metres, shelves thirteen metres high, around 70,000 books and some 600 magazine titles, open to anyone at no charge. Around it run the fashion, beauty and food-and-beverage floors, and the mall keeps one set of hours, 10:30 to 22:00.

You can reach all of it without going outside. Samseong Station on Line 2 connects directly through Exits 5 and 6 by way of Millennium Plaza, and Bongeunsa Station on Line 9 connects through Exit 7 by way of ASEM Plaza.

goto-mall.name: GOTO Mall
goto-mall.summary: The 620-shop arcade under the Express Bus Terminal — the largest of the 25 underground arcades the city operates.
goto-mall.bestFor: shopping without going outside, between the subway and the bus terminal
goto-mall.whyWeLikeIt: It is public infrastructure rather than a retail development — the Seoul Facilities Corporation runs it as one of 25 city-owned arcades, which is why the passageways stay open 24 hours whether or not the shops are.
goto-mall.longDescription:
GOTO Mall is the underground shopping arcade beneath the Express Bus Terminal in Seocho-gu, run by the Seoul Facilities Corporation as one of the 25 arcades the city owns. It covers 31,566 square metres and holds 620 shops, which makes it the largest of those 25 by both floor area and shop count.

The corporation lists its goods as clothing, flowers and household items, plus restaurants. Shops keep 10:00 to 22:00; the passageways themselves stay open 24 hours, so the arcade doubles as a route between the trains and the coaches.

Express Bus Terminal Station sits directly above it, served by Lines 3, 7 and 9, and the arcade links the station to the terminal building where buses leave for the rest of the country.

ipark-mall.name: I'Park Mall
ipark-mall.summary: The eleven-floor mall built into Yongsan Station — department store halls, an electronics centre, a cinema and an e-sports arena.
ipark-mall.bestFor: filling the hours before a train out of Yongsan Station
ipark-mall.whyWeLikeIt: It is built into Yongsan Station rather than near it, so the shops are reachable straight from the concourse without going outside.
ipark-mall.longDescription:
I'Park Mall stands at 55 Hangang-daero 23-gil and connects directly into Yongsan Station, which is the first thing to know about it — you reach the shops from the station without stepping outside.

Inside, it divides into the I'Park Department Store, itself split into Living, Culture and Fashion halls, plus a Digital Shopping Center and an Event Park. Alongside those are a CGV cinema, an e-sports stadium, an E-mart, a bookstore, a culture centre and more than a hundred restaurants, spread over eleven floors.

Hours run 10:30 to 20:30 Sunday through Thursday and 10:30 to 21:00 on Fridays and Saturdays, with floors one to three and the fashion park on four staying open to 22:00.

lotte-outlets-seoul-station.name: Lotte Outlets Seoul Station
lotte-outlets-seoul-station.summary: Three outlet floors inside the Seoul Station building, carrying 84 brands above a Lotte Mart.
lotte-outlets-seoul-station.bestFor: a shopping stop worked into a departure from Seoul Station
lotte-outlets-seoul-station.whyWeLikeIt: It is inside the station building rather than beside it, and the Lotte Mart below it stays open to 23:00 — two hours after the outlet floors have closed.
lotte-outlets-seoul-station.longDescription:
Lotte Outlets Seoul Station takes up three floors of the Seoul Station building at 405 Hangang-daero, in Jung-gu. It carries 84 brands across about 3,400 pyeong — roughly 11,000 square metres — among them the first North Face outlet store, and there are paid lockers on site for anyone shopping between trains.

The outlet floors run 10:30 to 21:00. Sharing the same building beneath them is a Lotte Mart branded Zettaplex, open 10:00 to 23:00 and closed two Wednesdays a month, with immediate tax refunds available to foreign shoppers.

ifc-mall.name: IFC Mall
ifc-mall.summary: Three basement levels under the International Finance Centre towers on Yeouido, reached from the station by a 360-metre moving walkway.
ifc-mall.bestFor: a cinema and a bookshop in the middle of the office district
ifc-mall.longDescription:
IFC Mall occupies three basement levels beneath the International Finance Centre at 10 Gukjegeumyung-ro, on Yeouido. It opened in 2012 and holds around 110 brands — fashion, beauty, sportswear and accessories — plus restaurants, a nine-screen CGV cinema and a Youngpoong Bookstore.

The approach is the distinctive part. A 360-metre moving walkway runs from Yeouido Station, where Lines 5 and 9 interchange, straight into the mall, so you never come up to street level.

Mall hours are 10:00 to 22:00; the street-level shops close an hour earlier, at 21:00.

common-ground.name: Common Ground
common-ground.summary: A complex assembled from 200 shipping containers outside Konkuk University, open since April 2015.
common-ground.bestFor: browsing a shopping complex built out of freight containers
common-ground.whyWeLikeIt: The containers aren't a decorative theme — the whole structure is 200 of them, stacked into two facing blocks.
common-ground.longDescription:
Common Ground stands at 200 Achasan-ro in Gwangjin-gu, built from 200 shipping containers and open since 10 April 2015. The containers are stacked into two facing blocks, Street Market and Market Hall, and the complex's other named zones are a Culture Space, a Terrace Market and a Market Ground.

Street Market holds thirty shops and Market Hall carries 26 boutique brands, with an Adidas Originals store occupying a zone of its own.

Opening hours are 11:00 to 22:00, with some of the third-floor food tenants running to 01:00 at weekends. Konkuk University Station, where Lines 2 and 7 meet, is Exit 3 and about three minutes away on foot.

myeongdong-underground-shopping-center.name: Myeongdong Underground Shopping Center
myeongdong-underground-shopping-center.summary: A 61-shop arcade under Namdaemun-ro listed for eyewear and clothing — and entered from Euljiro 1-ga Station, not Myeongdong Station.
myeongdong-underground-shopping-center.bestFor: eyeglasses, and a covered route between Euljiro and Myeongdong
myeongdong-underground-shopping-center.whyWeLikeIt: The operator gives its main goods as eyeglasses and clothing, and the name misleads on access: the entrance is at Euljiro 1-ga, while the arcade under Myeongdong Station is a different one.
myeongdong-underground-shopping-center.longDescription:
The Myeongdong Underground Shopping Center runs under Namdaemun-ro at basement number 72, one of the 25 underground arcades the Seoul Facilities Corporation operates. It covers 3,838 square metres and holds 61 shops; the operator lists its main goods as eyeglasses and clothing.

The name is misleading about how you get in. The arcade connects to Euljiro 1-ga Station on Line 2, at Exit 7 — not to Myeongdong Station. There is a separate arcade at Myeongdong Station on Line 4, running under Toegye-ro with 70 shops of its own selling clothing, bags and accessories.

Shops open 09:00 to 22:00 and the arcade trades year-round; the passageway itself stays open 24 hours.

apm-place.name: Apm Place
apm-place.summary: A twelve-storey wholesale fashion building in Dongdaemun that trades overnight, from 8pm to 5am, and closes at weekends.
apm-place.bestFor: buying women's clothing wholesale on Dongdaemun's night schedule
apm-place.whyWeLikeIt: Its hours say what it is: 8pm to 5am, shut Friday and Saturday. This building runs on the buyers' week, not the shopper's weekend.
apm-place.longDescription:
apM PLACE is at 276 Euljiro, one of three apM buildings in Dongdaemun — with apM and apM Luxe — that trade as wholesale fashion malls.

The selling floors are given over almost entirely to women's clothing, filling floors one through eight and the first basement, with miscellaneous goods on the second basement. Above the shop floors the building turns over to storage on nine, offices on ten, and officetels on eleven and twelve; parking sits on basement levels four and five.

Trading runs from 8:00pm to 5:00am the following morning, and the building is closed on Fridays and Saturdays. That is the Dongdaemun wholesale cycle rather than an ordinary mall's timetable, so anyone arriving in the daytime will find the shutters down.

stylenanda-pink-hotel-flagship-store.name: Stylenanda Pink Hotel Flagship Store
stylenanda-pink-hotel-flagship-store.summary: Stylenanda's Myeongdong flagship — a store fitted out to look like a hotel, carrying the brand's 3CE cosmetics line.
stylenanda-pink-hotel-flagship-store.bestFor: 3CE cosmetics bought at the brand's own flagship
stylenanda-pink-hotel-flagship-store.longDescription:
The Stylenanda Pink Hotel is the brand's Myeongdong flagship, at 37-8 Myeongdong 8-gil in Jung-gu, and has been open since October 2016. Seoul's official tourism listing describes it as a store fitted out to look like a hotel — the conceit its name refers to.

What it carries is the brand's own range, including 3CE, the cosmetics line Nanda launched in 2004.

It opens at 12:00 and closes at 21:00. Myeongdong Station Exit 6, on Line 4, is 148 metres away.

mecenatpolis-mall.name: Mecenatpolis Mall
mecenatpolis-mall.summary: An open-air street mall at the foot of the Mecenatpolis towers in Hapjeong, connected directly to the station.
mecenatpolis-mall.bestFor: a cinema, a supermarket and a meal without an enclosed mall around them
mecenatpolis-mall.whyWeLikeIt: A Lotte Cinema and a performance venue, the Lotte Card Art Center, are built into the same complex as the shops and the supermarket.
mecenatpolis-mall.longDescription:
Mecenatpolis Mall sits at 45 Yanghwa-ro in Seogyo-dong, at the base of the Mecenatpolis complex — three residential towers plus offices, completed in 2012. The Korea Tourism Organization classifies the mall itself as a street mall, meaning its shops line open walkways rather than enclosed corridors.

Tenants cover fashion and beauty, a large supermarket, and a run of restaurants and cafés. A Lotte Cinema is on site, as is the Lotte Card Art Center, a performance venue.

The mall connects directly to Hapjeong Station, where Lines 2 and 6 interchange.

garden-5.name: Garden 5
garden-5.summary: A four-hall retail complex at Jangji Station, built by the city to rehouse traders displaced by the Cheonggyecheon restoration.
garden-5.bestFor: a full-day mall trip in southeastern Seoul
garden-5.whyWeLikeIt: Roughly 4,000 retail units sit across its four halls, anchored by an NC Department Store, a Hyundai City Mall outlet and a CGV multiplex.
garden-5.longDescription:
Garden 5 is at 66 Chungmin-ro in Munjeong-dong, in southeastern Seoul. Songpa-gu's own listing describes four halls — Fashion, Main, Living and Techno — holding roughly 4,000 retail units between them.

The complex exists because of the Cheonggyecheon restoration. Seoul's city government, through its SH Corporation, developed it as somewhere the traders cleared from the stream's banks could reopen, and it opened in June 2010.

The large tenants today are an NC Department Store, a Hyundai City Mall urban outlet and a CGV multiplex. Hours are 10:30 to 21:00 Monday to Thursday and 10:30 to 22:00 Friday to Sunday, with the food halls running 10:00 to 23:00 every day. Jangji Station on Line 8 is Exit 4.

nampyeonghwa-sangga.name: Nampyeonghwa Sangga
nampyeonghwa-sangga.summary: A wholesale market for bags and clothing on the Dongdaemun edge of Jung-gu, trading since 1980 across a basement and three floors.
nampyeonghwa-sangga.bestFor: bags bought wholesale, on the market's own hours
nampyeonghwa-sangga.whyWeLikeIt: Bags are the specialism rather than a side line: the basement and the whole ground floor are given to them, in a building that has been trading since 1980.
nampyeonghwa-sangga.longDescription:
Nampyeonghwa Sangga is a wholesale market for bags and clothing at 282-10 Jangchungdan-ro, in Sindang-dong on the Dongdaemun side of Jung-gu. It has been trading since 1980 and holds around 700 shops across a basement and three floors.

Stock is arranged by level: bags in the basement and on the ground floor, young casual wear on the second floor, denim and women's clothing on the third.

The hours split the same way. The basement and ground floor trade from midnight to noon; the second and third floors trade from 8:00pm to 5:00am. The whole building is closed on Fridays and Saturdays, and on the days it does open, no floor trades in the afternoon.

hello-apm.name: Hello APM
hello-apm.summary: A Dongdaemun fashion building that trades retail rather than wholesale, with the clothing on its lower four floors — open to 1am, closed Tuesdays.
hello-apm.bestFor: late-evening clothes shopping in Dongdaemun without wholesale hours
hello-apm.whyWeLikeIt: Only part of the building is a mall. Clothing occupies the basement and floors one to four; five to seven are listed as vacant, and everything above is a gym, clinics and offices.
hello-apm.longDescription:
Hello apm is at 253 Jangchungdan-ro in Dongdaemun. The Dongdaemun Fashion Town tourist-zone directory lists it as a shopping centre and discount store rather than a wholesale building, and the hours match: 10:20 in the morning until 1:00am, closed on Tuesdays.

Clothing sits on the lower floors — women's wear on one, two and three, with women's accessories on three; children's wear and wedding goods, including hanbok, bedding, jewellery and curtains, also on two; men's wear and accessories on four. The basement carries shoes, imported cosmetics, tourist goods and a comics café, and there is a pharmacy on the ground floor.

Floors five to seven are listed as vacant. The floors above them are not retail at all: a gym on eight, screen golf and billiards on nine, dental, paediatric, obstetric and dermatology clinics on ten, and management offices on eleven.

myeongdong-migliore.name: Myeongdong Migliore
myeongdong-migliore.summary: Two retail floors at Myeongdong Station Exit 6, under fifteen storeys of hotel — remodelled and reopened in August 2024.
myeongdong-migliore.bestFor: a short stop right outside Myeongdong Station Exit 6
myeongdong-migliore.whyWeLikeIt: It sits directly at Myeongdong Station Exit 6, and what's on its two floors is a mix rather than a category — an Olive Young, a handful of fashion labels, a K-pop merchandise shop and cafés.
myeongdong-migliore.longDescription:
Myeongdong Migliore is at 115 Toegye-ro, directly in front of Myeongdong Station Exit 6. Migliore opened its first branch in Dongdaemun in February 1998 and this Myeongdong branch in 2000.

The building now does two jobs at once. Floors one and two are the shopping mall; floors three to seventeen operate as a hotel. The two retail floors were remodelled and reopened in August 2024.

What's on them is a mix rather than one category: Olive Young and Giordano, fashion labels including Folder, Roem, Drawfit and Instant Punk, the K-pop merchandise shop AllThatKpop, and cafés. Opening hours are set store by store rather than for the building, so each shop keeps its own.

Its rating stands at 3.1 across 42 ratings — a small sample.

spa-gogyeol.name: Spa Gogyeol
spa-gogyeol.summary: Cheongdam treatment spa worked entirely by hand, with a second branch in Seocho.
spa-gogyeol.bestFor: a hands-only Korean manual therapy session
spa-gogyeol.longDescription:
Spa Gogyeol is at 13 Seolleung-ro 132-gil in Cheongdam, a private treatment spa rather than a bathhouse. The description it gives of its own work is a narrow one: care worked entirely by the therapist's hands, in the Korean sugi manual-therapy tradition, read from each client's skin and muscle rather than run off a fixed course.

The business runs two branches — this one and a second in Seocho, at 42 Seocho-jungang-ro. Booking for either goes through Naver, KakaoTalk or Instagram rather than one central page. The Cheongdam address is a fourth-floor unit.

aroma-thai-spa-gongdeok.name: Aroma Thai Spa Gongdeok
aroma-thai-spa-gongdeok.summary: Thai spa in a basement unit of the Taeyoung Desian complex, in Mapo-gu's Gongdeok area.
aroma-thai-spa-gongdeok.bestFor: a Thai spa appointment in the Gongdeok area
aroma-thai-spa-gongdeok.longDescription:
Aroma Thai Spa occupies unit B101, a basement space in the Taeyoung Desian complex at 320 Dokmak-ro in Mapo-gu, in the Gongdeok area.

It is listed as a Thai spa, and that is as far as the published record goes — no treatment menu, no price list, and no operator site we could open. A phone number is listed, which is the practical way in.

Published opening hours differ between listings, so confirm the closing time before you plan around it.

lavish-spa.name: Lavish Spa
lavish-spa.summary: Second-floor massage studio on Dongsung 3-gil in Jongno.
lavish-spa.longDescription:
Lavish Spa is a massage studio on the second floor at 6-4 Dongsung 3-gil, in Jongno-gu.

It publishes a phone number and an Instagram account, @lavishspa, and little else — no treatment menu, no price list, no site of its own. That makes it a place to call before you go rather than one to plan a day around. Ask what a course covers and confirm the hours; neither is published anywhere we could check.

2s-apgujeong.name: 2s Apgujeong
2s-apgujeong.summary: Listed as a spa on Seolleung-ro 157-gil in Apgujeong, with almost nothing published about it.
2s-apgujeong.bestFor: confirming what is offered before booking
2s-apgujeong.longDescription:
2s is listed as a spa on the fourth floor at 6 Seolleung-ro 157-gil, in Apgujeong.

We could not find anything published about it beyond that address — no operator page, no treatment menu, no tourism or trade listing. The entry stays unverified on that basis, and is not published in the directory. Confirm what is offered, and at what price, before booking.

marzia-healing-spa-cheongdam.name: Marzia Healing Spa - Cheongdam
marzia-healing-spa-cheongdam.summary: Cheongdam day spa working by appointment, with a programme range from facials to scalp and men's care.
marzia-healing-spa-cheongdam.bestFor: a booked day-spa course in Cheongdam
marzia-healing-spa-cheongdam.longDescription:
Marzia Healing Spa's Cheongdam branch is a day spa that works by appointment rather than walk-in.

The programme range covers facial care, body care, scalp care and a separate men's line, plus sugaring hair removal, and courses built around particular circumstances — wedding preparation, pregnancy, and treatments for children. Korea's national tourism organisation describes the approach as traditional Korean practice combined with European aromatherapy technique.

We are not listing an address for this branch. Two official listings give different ones and we could not confirm either as current, so ask for the address when you book, and confirm the course at the same time.

provence-spa-by-loccitane.name: Provence Spa by L'OCCITANE
provence-spa-by-loccitane.summary: L'OCCITANE's spa inside the JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square, bookable whether or not you are staying.
provence-spa-by-loccitane.bestFor: a French-brand facial and body course in Dongdaemun
provence-spa-by-loccitane.whyWeLikeIt: The hotel opens it to non-residents, so the spa is bookable on its own — you do not have to be a guest to use it.
provence-spa-by-loccitane.longDescription:
Provence Spa is the L'OCCITANE-branded spa inside the JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square Seoul, at 279 Cheonggyecheon-ro in Jongno-gu.

It works with the French brand's own oils and plant extracts. The menu covers facials, hair and scalp treatments, body scrubs, wraps and massages, with couples' treatments as an option. The signature course, the Immortelle Divine Journey to Perfection, pairs an anti-ageing facial with shoulder, back and foot massage, using organic immortelle and myrtle.

Both hotel guests and non-residents can book. The hotel's other wellness facilities — a 25-metre indoor lap pool and the Club 501 fitness centre — are separate from the spa.

the-spa-grand-hyatt-seoul.name: The Spa Grand Hyatt Seoul
the-spa-grand-hyatt-seoul.summary: The Grand Hyatt's own spa, on the hotel's garden level in Yongsan-gu.
the-spa-grand-hyatt-seoul.bestFor: a hotel spa treatment away from street level
the-spa-grand-hyatt-seoul.longDescription:
The Spa occupies the garden level of the Grand Hyatt Seoul, at 322 Sowol-ro in Yongsan-gu, about five minutes' drive from the Itaewon shopping district. It opened in April 2007.

Treatments are taken in spa suites and treatment rooms, and the menu runs to massages, facials, body treatments, scrubs and wraps.

It is a separate operation from Club Olympus, the hotel's fitness centre, which has its own men's and women's saunas with a Korean body-scrub service, plus indoor, outdoor and children's pools. Published opening hours differ between sources, so confirm them rather than planning a day around them.

spa-1899-donginbi.name: Spa 1899 Donginbi
spa-1899-donginbi.summary: Red-ginseng spa run by the Donginbi skincare brand, two levels beneath KT&G Tower in Gangnam.
spa-1899-donginbi.bestFor: a red-ginseng treatment course near Samseong Station
spa-1899-donginbi.whyWeLikeIt: The ginseng is not a theme laid over a generic menu. The spa belongs to Donginbi, the skincare line that grew out of the Cheong Kwan Jang red-ginseng business, and its signature course is built on the same material.
spa-1899-donginbi.longDescription:
Spa 1899 is on the second basement level of KT&G Tower, at 416 Yeongdong-daero in Gangnam-gu, about nine minutes on foot from Exit 2 of Samseong Station on Line 2.

It is run by Donginbi, the skincare line that grew out of the Cheong Kwan Jang red-ginseng business, and its treatments are built on that red ginseng. The signature course, Red Ginseng Energy Circulation Therapy, is the spa's own. Around it sit single-focus programmes of an hour each — facial, body or foot — multi-care courses of two to two and a half hours, and a three-hour full peeling.

Parking is free for guests. Published opening hours differ between the operator's own page and the tourism listing, so confirm the last appointment when you book.

asuca.name: Asuca
asuca.summary: Spa listed on Jangchungdan-ro in Jung-gu, with almost nothing published about it.
asuca.bestFor: confirming what is offered before booking
asuca.longDescription:
Asuca is listed as a spa at 213 Jangchungdan-ro, in Jung-gu near Dongdaemun.

Beyond the name and the address we found nothing published about it — no operator page, no treatment menu, no tourism or trade listing, in Korean or in English. With no way to establish what the business offers, the entry stays unverified and is not published in the directory.

bamboo-therapy.name: Bamboo Therapy
bamboo-therapy.summary: Foot-and-body massage shop in Hapjeong whose current operation we could not confirm.
bamboo-therapy.bestFor: confirming by phone before you go
bamboo-therapy.longDescription:
Bamboo Therapy is listed as a foot-and-body massage shop at 22 Yanghwa-ro 18an-gil, in the Hapjeong area of Mapo-gu.

We could not establish whether it still trades. There is no operator page, no current Korean-language business listing that matches the address, and the material still online about it is several years old.

The entry stays unverified on that basis and is not published in the directory. Do not plan a visit around it without confirming first that it is open.

gold-spa.name: Gold Spa
gold-spa.summary: Jjimjilbang two levels beneath the Lotte Castle Benecia complex on Cheonggyecheon-ro, open around the clock.
gold-spa.bestFor: a communal bathhouse rather than a private treatment room
gold-spa.longDescription:
Gold Spa is on the second basement level of the Lotte Castle Benecia complex, at 400 Cheonggyecheon-ro in the Hwanghak-dong part of Jung-gu — the same block as a supermarket and a cinema.

It is a jjimjilbang rather than a private spa: the communal bathhouse format, shared bathing and heated rooms rather than a treatment table booked in your name. A restaurant and a shop sit on the same floor, along with a doctor-fish tank charged separately.

It runs 24 hours a day, year round, priced as a day rate and a night rate rather than by the hour, and it does not take reservations — you pay at the desk on arrival. Parking under the building comes with four hours free.

supsok-hanbang-land.name: Supsok Hanbang Land
supsok-hanbang-land.summary: Oak-charcoal kiln bathhouse at the foot of Ansan, reached by bus from Sinchon.
supsok-hanbang-land.bestFor: the charcoal-kiln version of a Korean sauna
supsok-hanbang-land.whyWeLikeIt: A charcoal kiln is a different heat from a jjimjilbang's heated room. The kilns here are held at low, medium and high temperatures, so you work through them in stages rather than picking one and staying in it.
supsok-hanbang-land.longDescription:
Supsok Hanbang Land is at 75-7 Bongwonsa-gil, in Bongwon-dong, on the Seodaemun side of Ansan and next to Bongwonsa temple.

The format is the charcoal kiln rather than the jjimjilbang: domed kilns fired with oak charcoal and held at low, medium and high temperatures. Men's and women's bathhouses are separate. There is a restaurant on site, and a fire pit at the kilns where sweet potatoes and rice cakes are roasted.

The grounds open at 06:30 and close at 22:00; the kilns themselves run from 08:00 to 21:00. Getting there means a bus — Sinchon Station on Line 2, then the bus towards Bongwonsa — and the Ansan trails start from the same spot.

sparex-sauna.name: SPAREX Sauna (Dongmyo)
sparex-sauna.summary: The Sparex chain's Dongmyo branch — open 24 hours, directly outside Dongmyoap Station Exit 6.
sparex-sauna.bestFor: a 24-hour sauna next to a subway exit
sparex-sauna.longDescription:
This is the Dongmyo branch of Sparex, in the Season Building at 19 Jibong-ro, Changsin-dong, in Jongno-gu. It is not the chain's Good Morning City branch, which is a separate site at 247 Jangchungdan-ro in Jung-gu, by Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station.

The Dongmyo branch is open 24 hours, year round, and stands directly outside Exit 6 of Dongmyoap Station, where Lines 1 and 6 meet. Inside are wet and dry saunas, a food court, sleeping areas, and a body-scrub service running day and night. The fit-out is modern — white surfaces and wood — rather than the traditional hanok-style interior the Good Morning City branch is known for.

Luggage storage is available, which makes it usable on a travel day.

riverside-spa-land.name: Riverside Spa Land
riverside-spa-land.summary: Traditional pine-fired kiln bathhouse over two basement levels in Gwangjin.
riverside-spa-land.bestFor: the wood-fired end of Korean sauna culture
riverside-spa-land.whyWeLikeIt: The main heat source is a pine-log fire rather than an element — the older bulhanjeungmak method — and the rooms around it are graded by material as much as by temperature: charcoal, salt, ochre, silver.
riverside-spa-land.longDescription:
Riverside Spa Land occupies two basement levels at 45 Guui-gangbyeon-ro in Gwangjin-gu, about 9,900 square metres in all.

The centrepiece is a traditional bulhanjeungmak, a kiln heated by burning pine logs rather than by an element. Around it are rooms graded by material: charcoal, salt, a silver pyramid room, ochre rooms, an igloo room, and an ochre kiln reserved for women. The wet side has hot and cold pools, a massage pool, an aqua-walking pool and both wet and dry saunas, drawn on sulphur groundwater.

It is open around the clock, year round, with admission split into a daytime and a night rate. Game rooms, a children's play area and food service sit alongside the bathing floors.

hokutosichisei.summary: Massage business listed on the fourth floor of an Euljiro office building, with nothing published about it.
hokutosichisei.bestFor: confirming what is offered before booking

hwangjok-massage.summary: Foot, body and aroma treatments on the fifth floor above a Lotteria in Myeongdong.
hwangjok-massage.unpublishedReason: 2.4★ across 19 ratings — held out of the directory on editorial judgment, kept for the record

The entry is kept for the record and is not published in the directory.

laurel-studio.name: Laurel Studio
laurel-studio.summary: K-beauty facial studio in Hongdae where the treatment is taken lying on a traditional ondol floor, from therapists in hanbok.
laurel-studio.whyWeLikeIt: There is no treatment bed. You lie on a traditional ondol floor, and the therapists work in remade hanbok.
laurel-studio.longDescription:
Laurel Studio is on the third floor at 7 World Cup-buk-ro, in Mapo-gu, about 250 metres from Exit 1 of Hongik University Station.

What sets the treatment apart is where it happens: rather than a treatment bed, you lie on a traditional ondol floor, and the therapists work in remade hanbok. Every session opens with a skin checklist, and the treatment is set from what it finds.

There are two programmes — a basic facial of about 50 minutes, and a premium version of about 60 that adds a skincare routine written for you and sent on afterwards. A session takes up to four people. The studio was founded by a former cosmetics ingredient researcher.

Booking is by WhatsApp or Instagram message, or through the studio's own booking page. English is available, and the studio provides foreign-language guide cards by country. Published opening hours differ between listings, so confirm your slot when you book.

dolce-far-niente.name: Dolce Far Niente
dolce-far-niente.summary: Skincare and spa room listed on the second floor at 93 Manrijae-ro in Mapo-gu.
dolce-far-niente.bestFor: confirming what is offered before booking
dolce-far-niente.longDescription:
Dolce Far Niente is listed as a spa on the second floor at 93 Manrijae-ro, in Mapo-gu, a short way from Gongdeok.

Beyond the name and the address we found nothing published about it in Korean or English: no operator page, no social account, no treatment menu, no price list and no opening hours. With no way to establish what the business offers, the entry stays unverified and is not published in the directory.

hera.name: Hera Este
hera.summary: Licensed skincare salon across three floors at 37 Myeongdong 8na-gil, two minutes from Myeongdong Station.
hera.bestFor: a korgi or hydration facial in Myeongdong
hera.whyWeLikeIt: Every course is published as an ordered list of steps rather than a name and a price, so you can see what a course consists of before you book.
hera.longDescription:
Hera Este occupies the third, fourth and fifth floors at 37 Myeongdong 8na-gil, in Jung-gu, about two minutes from Exit 10 of Myeongdong Station. Jung-gu's register of licensed beauty businesses records it there as a skincare premises. Map listings sometimes place it at the neighbouring number, 39, where the register records no beauty business at all.

The menu is short, and each course is published as an ordered sequence rather than a name. The facial line runs from a hydration course — scalp work, cleanse and deep cleanse, facial and neck lymph drainage, a hyaluronic mask — to a korgi course that swaps the cleansing steps for bone-pressing work on the face. Longer courses add a foot spa, exfoliation, a vitamin or gold pack and leg drainage; body courses cover the back, the feet and the whole body.

It is worked by a single practitioner, a licensed esthetician of fifteen years. Published opening hours differ between listings, so confirm the time when you book.

mizo-esthe-salon.name: MIZO Esthe Salon
mizo-esthe-salon.summary: Myeongdong esthetic salon built around korgi facial work, a couple of minutes from the station.
mizo-esthe-salon.bestFor: a korgi facial or a body course near Myeongdong Station
mizo-esthe-salon.whyWeLikeIt: Its facial work is built on korgi, the Korean bone-pressing massage, and can be taken on its own or paired with a body course.
mizo-esthe-salon.longDescription:
MIZO Esthe Salon is at 66-9 Chungmuro 2-ga, in Jung-gu, a couple of minutes from Exit 6 of Myeongdong Station on Line 4.

The menu covers more than facial work. The facial course is built on korgi, the Korean bone-pressing massage, and finishes with a pack; alongside it sit full-body massage, a back detox with a hot pack, foot massage and reflexology, air massage and a paraffin pack. Korgi can be booked on its own or with body work added. Couple rooms are available, and the salon takes cards.

The salon's own web address no longer resolves, and it does not appear on Jung-gu's register of licensed beauty businesses, so travel listings are the only published source for its details — and they do not agree. The floor is given as both the fourth and the eighth, and the closing time as anywhere from 22:00 to midnight. Bookings run through Japanese travel agencies as well as directly. Confirm the floor, the hours and the price when you reserve.

seoulistique-skin.name: Seoulistique Skin
seoulistique-skin.summary: K-beauty skincare studio at Aeogae Station, booked by message rather than through a site.
seoulistique-skin.bestFor: a non-invasive facial near Aeogae Station
seoulistique-skin.longDescription:
Seoulistique Skin is a skincare studio in Mapo-gu, at Exit 2 of Aeogae Station.

It describes its own work narrowly: non-invasive K-beauty skincare treatments. The studio previously traded as Fleur Jardin, and that account now points to this one.

There is no website, no published menu and no price list. Booking is by Instagram message or WhatsApp, and no opening hours are published, so agree a time when you book.

sulwhasoo-spa.name: Sulwhasoo Spa (Lotte Hotel Seoul)
sulwhasoo-spa.summary: Amorepacific's Sulwhasoo spa, on the seventh floor of the Lotte Hotel Seoul main building in Jung-gu.
sulwhasoo-spa.bestFor: a ginseng-based facial course in central Jung-gu
sulwhasoo-spa.whyWeLikeIt: Each facial is worked with its own hand-held massager — nephrite jade, white porcelain, amber — rather than one tool used across the menu.
sulwhasoo-spa.longDescription:
Sulwhasoo Spa occupies the seventh floor of the main building of Lotte Hotel Seoul, at 30 Euljiro in Jung-gu. It is not the brand's flagship-store spa in Gangnam, which is a separate operation at 18 Dosan-daero 45-gil. This one moved up from the hotel's third and fourth floors and reopened on 1 October 2018 after a redesign.

The menu splits three ways. Facials run from the Moisturizing & Comforting and Calming & Vitalizing treatments through to the Signature Ginseng and The Ultimate S, at 80 to 90 minutes each; body care comes in recovery, circulation and intensive forms of 50 to 90 minutes; and the journeys pair a facial with body work over 100 to 180 minutes.

It opens 10:30 to 21:00 daily, closing on the first Monday of each month and on Seollal and Chuseok. The hotel is being rebranded as The Grand Lotte Seoul, so confirm the spa's arrangements when you book.

individuel-geneve.name: Inko Seoul (formerly Individuel Genève)
individuel-geneve.summary: Skin-analysis-led facial studio near Gangnam-gu Office Station, now trading as Inko Seoul.
individuel-geneve.bestFor: a facial assembled from a digital skin analysis
individuel-geneve.whyWeLikeIt: The course is built from a digital skin scan read across six measures, and the scan is repeated as treatment progresses rather than taken once at the door.
individuel-geneve.longDescription:
Individuel Genève now trades as Inko Seoul. The studio is at 60 Bongeunsa-ro 47-gil in Gangnam-gu, about 600 metres from Exit 2 of Gangnam-gu Office Station; the old web address redirects to the new one, and the KakaoTalk booking channel still runs under the Individuel name.

The method starts with measurement. A digital analyser reads the skin across six points — type, oiliness, pores, spots, wrinkles and impurities — the treatment is assembled from what it returns, and the skin is scanned again as the course runs so the plan can be adjusted.

What gets assembled draws on a published set of technologies: dual-wave ultrasound, magnetic infusion, microneedling with skin boosters, cold plasma, ear seeds, air-therapy lymphatic drainage and LED, worked with active formulas including exosome, NAD+, PDRN, vitamin C and azelaic acid. Colour analysis is offered separately.

No opening hours are published. Booking goes through the site's form, WhatsApp or KakaoTalk.

stone-house-head-spa.summary: Head spa listed on a basement level off Eonju-ro 147-gil in Gangnam, with nothing published about it.

eco-jardin-aeogae-branch.name: Eco Jardin (Aeogae)
eco-jardin-aeogae-branch.summary: The Eco Jardin group's Aeogae branch — a hair salon whose head spa runs to a published fifteen- or eighteen-step scalp programme.
eco-jardin-aeogae-branch.bestFor: a step-by-step scalp treatment near Aeogae Station
eco-jardin-aeogae-branch.whyWeLikeIt: The scalp programme is published step by step, and the scalp is read under a microscope at the start and again near the end — so the before and after is something you look at.
eco-jardin-aeogae-branch.longDescription:
This is the Aeogae branch of Eco Jardin, on the second floor of the Mapo SK Hub Blue building at 204 Mapo-daero, in Ahyeon-dong, Mapo-gu. It is not the group's Jongno branch, a separate premises at 9 Jahamun-ro near Gyeongbokgung, nor the Jamsil one; Eco Jardin runs several salons in Seoul and franchises the name.

The branch is registered as a beauty business, was established in February 2024 and takes four units on its floor. It carries the group's main Instagram account, which names it the Aeogae flagship, and bookings are taken by direct message or WhatsApp rather than by phone.

The head spa here comes in two lengths. Both open with a microscope reading of the scalp and take a second one three steps from the end; between them run neck work and suction, a hot towel, an aroma-oil cleanse and a scrub, steam, shampoo, and tonic and stick treatments. The eighteen-step version adds a scalp massage, a herbal pack and a steam cap to the fifteen.

create-wellness-center.name: Create Wellness Center
create-wellness-center.summary: Chiropractic and rehabilitation clinic on Itaewon-ro, working in English since 2001.
create-wellness-center.bestFor: English-language treatment for back, neck or joint pain
create-wellness-center.whyWeLikeIt: It is a clinic rather than a treatment room: chiropractic, rehabilitation, therapeutic massage, naturopathy and osteopathy under one roof, in English as well as Korean.
create-wellness-center.longDescription:
Create Wellness Center is on the ground floor of the Hannam Building at 211 Itaewon-ro, in Yongsan-gu, near Exit 2 of Itaewon Station.

It is a clinic rather than a gym or a spa. The work is US chiropractic, rehabilitation, therapeutic massage, visceral osteopathy, naturopathy and nutritional consultation, with mat pilates run as group exercise alongside. The centre has worked with Korea's foreign community since 2001, with internationally trained practitioners and bilingual staff, and it runs a second branch on Jeju.

Hours are 09:00 to 19:00 on weekdays and 09:00 to 18:00 at weekends, with the clinic closed between 13:00 and 14:00. Appointments go through the Mindbody app, by phone or email, or by message on Instagram or Facebook.
